name: Scope as the room object, resolved once per turn
what: Every conversation maps to one scope (a DM to personal:<person>, a channel or group DM to channel:<id> or group:<id>, plus team and org scopes). The scope owns the memory, files, crons, apps, sandbox and credentials view that the agent sees in that room.
how: ScopeId is a 'kind:ref' string with five kinds (personal, channel, team, org, group). conversationScope() maps dm to personal(actor), group to group:ref, else channel:ref. createResolutionService().resolve() returns one Resolution object: workspace layers, composed system prompt, egress floor, command policy, security policy, sharing posture, approval grant modes and granted resource handles. Config is refreshed from the durable store before each resolve.
verevonRelevance: Matches the Space direction: one resolver that returns every policy layer for the active room is the adoptable part, but Verevon must keep typed SpaceRef and Control-issued decisions instead of QM's string-encoded kind:ref ids.
notes: Quality 4: coherent and widely reused, but the resolver is fed by scope-config stores that are partly process-cached (config.refreshSecurity before resolve). The 2026-08 Verevon comparison already lists this as the top QM strength; unchanged and still present on 2026-10-12.

name: Agent acts as the speaking human, not as its own principal
what: In a room the agent runs with the authority of the person whose message triggered the turn (their credentials, grants and approvals), and every action is audited under that person. The agent has no member identity of its own in a channel.
how: TurnRequest carries actor (ActorAssertion) and audience; the actor is classified by IdentityService and stamped into capability tokens as actorId/liveActor. README states the agent acts as the person it works for. Unattended work uses runAs modes (owner, scopeFloor, scopeShared) instead of an agent principal.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already models agents as Control service-subject members with their own authority; QM's delegate-as-human model is simpler but makes shared-room attribution and revocation weaker. Keep the Verevon model and borrow only the fire-time recheck.
notes: Quality 3: it is simple and auditable, but the SECURITY.md limitations (credentials plaintext in sandbox, purposes not enforced) follow directly from agents wielding a human identity.

name: Tighten-only policy cascade (org floor, scope may only narrow)
what: An org sets the floor for security posture, command policy and sharing posture; rooms and people can only make it stricter. Deployment tool descriptors can add deny or require-approval rules but never an allow.
how: composeSecurityPosture() takes the higher rank of org floor and scope; composePolicy() appends scope rules after org rules and forces allowlist mode if the org is allowlist; composeSharingPosture() lets Isolated win; tool descriptor 'approvals' are appended to the floor and cannot loosen it.
verevonRelevance: Directly applicable to the Platform to org to Space instruction/policy hierarchy in the Verevon plan; enforce it as a monotone merge function with tests, as QM does.
notes: Quality 4: composition rules are small, pure and tested (test/security-posture.test.ts, test/command-policy.test.ts); weakened by the admin setter that can replace floors (see command-policy record). Ratchet-only extension (manifests cannot add allow rules) is the part worth copying into Verevon agent bindings and capability manifests.

name: Audience-intersection floor for egress and resource grants
what: In a shared room the allowed outbound hosts are the intersection of what every participant may reach, denied hosts are the union, and granted resources are only those every participant is entitled to.
how: audienceEgressFloor() intersects per-principal allowed-host sets (org, scope, personal, team scopes); audienceDeniedFloor() unions denied hosts; acl.handlesForAudience() applies principalEntitledToScope for granted file/skill/deploy/cron/service-cred handles.
verevonRelevance: Maps onto Verevon's 'Space decision intersect recipient audience intersect owner-plane ACL' rule; the explicit least-common-denominator computation is a ready template for retrieval, tools and egress in a Space.
notes: Quality 4: intersection logic is explicit and tested in test/audience-floor.test.ts; model discretion after authorization is still outside it (SECURITY.md). Union-for-deny and intersection-for-allow is the correct fail-closed shape. Known gap per SECURITY.md:163: the ambient Slack judge path does not repeat the full internal-only check.

name: Provenance label on every transcript entry, audience-filtered read
what: Each stored entry carries the scope it came from (a personal tool result read inside a channel keeps its personal label); when the agent speaks to a room, only entries every listener is entitled to are shown to the model.
how: classifyScopeLabel() stamps scopeLabel (soul entries get the org scope, tool results get the source scope, everything else the session scope); filterHistoryForAudience() keeps an entry only if every audience member is entitled to its label; the tape spec formalizes this as context = fold(tape, audience).
verevonRelevance: Equivalent to the Verevon plan to bind a recipient-audience revision to each entry; QM shows the write-time label plus read-time fold is cheap (sub-ms fold, 5KB p50 session) and testable (test/scope-reach.test.ts).
notes: Quality 4: every entry carries a label and reads are filtered (test/agent-transcript-memory-boundary.test.ts), but SECURITY.md admits labels are incomplete for some granted reads. SECURITY.md:163 admits model-context entries do not yet carry complete origin labels for every granted read, so mixed-permission filtering is incomplete.

name: Fixed small agent tool catalog organized by resource and action
what: The agent sees one compact tool surface (execute, sandbox, background, read, write, files, skills, memory, history, subagents, sessions, cron, webhook, publish, share, goal tools, a surface tool for Slack or web, admin) instead of hundreds of integrations; integrations are reached through the shell and an HTTP self-API.
how: agent-tools.ts defines the catalog with literal tool names (execute at 876/894/918, sandbox 932, skill 1069, memory 1314, publish 1200, subagents 1529, background 1932, cron 2280, webhook 2770). Commit 99ff48fb reorganized tools by resource and action; execute became the sole command launcher (a40bc891).
verevonRelevance: Supports the Verevon plan not to reduce typed business actions to shell: QM's pattern is a thin fixed tool shell plus a discoverable typed API, which Verevon can mirror with the owner-approved Action Catalog as the API half.
notes: Quality 4: one tool catalog for every harness, tested in test/agent-tools.test.ts; the file is 4,600 lines and tool count keeps growing. agent-tools.ts is 4,602 lines (god-file lens in docs/SPEC.md:119-126). Tool names are literals found by grep; some definitions are conditional on flags (persistent_subagents, responsive_spine).

name: Agent self-API catalog (/v1/apis), one API for UI and agent
what: From inside its computer the agent calls the same REST API the UI uses, authenticated with its per-turn capability token, and can discover what it may call from a catalog filtered by its token, admin status and feature flags.
how: agent-api-catalog.ts defines FAMILIES of routes with match functions and a 'when' view predicate; agentApiMatches() gates which route paths a capability token may call; a parity test asserts every auth:either route is admitted and no source-only or public route is exposed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon wants human and agent actions to share one contract; QM's route-table-driven parity test is the concrete conformance gate to copy (route auth class versus agent-callable set).
notes: Quality 3: parity tests pin the agent-callable route set (test/agent-api-parity.test.ts); the allowlist is still a hand-maintained family table. docs/SPEC.md:145-153 lists this allowlist as a regex chain (regex lens, qm#169) rather than matching the router's declared routes. Quality 3 for that reason.

name: Four swappable agent harnesses behind one adapter contract
what: A deployment or a scope can run turns on Pi, OpenCode, Codex or Claude Code (plus a mock) without changing tools, memory or approvals; the harness choice is a runtime setting with the model and effort.
how: defineHarness(profile, implementation) with HarnessAdapterProfile (controlTransport, toolTransport, transcriptFormat, capabilities set: abort, steer, images, thinking-level, fast-mode, provider-sessions, native-tape, goal-enforcement). The Claude adapter sets built-in tools to none and bridges QM tools through an in-process SDK MCP server; Codex runs approvalPolicy never with sandbox read-only and dynamicTools; OpenCode loads a plugin. Goal enforcement is applied in harness-router for every harness.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon baseline already recommends a typed runtime-adapter profile with native effects disabled; QM shows the working shape (capability set per adapter, governed tools presented through each harness's native extension point).
notes: Quality 4: four real adapters with parity work, but SPEC lists provider drift and config-matrix growth as recurring costs.

name: Helper-model utilities as part of the harness contract
what: The same harness supplies cheap side calls used around turns: should-respond detection, history compaction, one-shot text, judge, security screen, ack-emoji pick, title generation and a plain-language summary of an approval request.
how: HarnessModelUtilities exposes shouldRespond, compactHistory, contextTokenBudget, oneShot, judge, screenSecurity, pickAckEmoji, generateTitle and summarizeApproval; a configurable helper model (Haiku-class per commit bca3b27f) serves them.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space needs the same cheap-judge slot for ambient decisions, approval summaries and titles; define it once in the Model Plane adapter profile rather than per feature.
notes: Quality 3: useful helper surface but thin: the helper model is a single configured model with no fallback logic noted. Model ids per commit subject only (DOC git), not verified in config.

name: Durable command approvals with grant modes (once, session, always)
what: When a gated command needs a human, the platform stores a pending approval, shows a card in the originating thread or DM, and resumes the turn on Run or Deny. Org policy decides whether session-wide and standing approvals are allowed.
how: PendingApprovalRecord is stored in a DurableMap; createApprovalStore().put() persists then enqueues a Slack delivery with idempotency key command-approval:<id>:<createdAt>; the id is hash(sessionId, command); ApprovalGrantModes {session, always} comes from the resolved scope; summarizeApproval gives a readable summary.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's room approvals record a grant but do not resume the paused run (baseline section 7); QM's persisted record plus atomic claim plus resume shows the missing half. Port the invariant (decision survives restart, delivered into the request thread), not the Slack card.
notes: Quality 4: persisted and idempotent (test/approval-store.test.ts, test/slack-approval-cards.test.ts); grant modes are simple and the Slack-first card flow is the polished path. Pending Slack approvals used to live in a process Map and were fixed in qm#963 (Non-durability lens, docs/SPEC.md:93).

name: Approval pause terminates generation; per-attempt interrupted-effect handling
what: When a tool call needs approval the model round stops immediately so the model cannot keep acting; on resume, a call whose result was lost is either re-run (if marked retrySafe) or reported to the model as 'outcome unknown, do not redo side effects'.
how: terminate:true is returned when ref.pausedOnApproval or a silent/handoff flag is set; tool schemas carry an optional retrySafe boolean and a recorded rerun input; the tape resume step appends an interrupt event for dangling calls; turn-resume.ts finds the trailing partial turn.
verevonRelevance: Both are P0 items in the Verevon QM adoption plan (approval pause ends the round, explicit interrupted-effect marker); the pointer pi-tools.ts:261-274 in that plan is stale, the code now lives in agent-tools.ts.
notes: Quality 4: interrupted effects are modelled explicitly and tested (test/tool-call-resume.test.ts, test/turn-resume.test.ts); retry-safe marking depends on each tool author. Corrects a baseline pointer: pi-tools.ts was folded into agent-tools.ts (git ba457a22, 2026-09-07).

name: Human-only authority walls (grants, impersonation, approval decisions)
what: Three decisions that authorize future agent behavior are deliberately absent from the agent API: changing admin grants, impersonating another principal, and approving a gated command or credential use.
how: SECURITY.md documents them as walls not gaps; the credential approval card is the only approval path for credential use (commit 1906e4af); parity tests pin the agent-callable route set.
verevonRelevance: Identical to the rule in docs/space-defenition.md that decisions authorizing future agent behavior come from outside the agent; keep it as an explicit negative test list in Verevon.
notes: Quality 5: clearly specified, enforced by route tables and tested.

name: Quarantine and one-time release of flagged tool output
what: If the injection screen flags content returned by a tool, the content is withheld from the model and a human sees a preview and can release it once or keep it blocked; release cannot become a standing grant.
how: Flagged results push a quarantineReleaseApprovals entry with approvalKey security-screen-release:<tool>, screenedOutput payload and grantModes {session:false, always:false}; audit actions security_posture.tool_result_quarantine and tool_result_release; the turn resumes with text saying the released content is data, not authority.
verevonRelevance: A human-visible quarantine with preview and single-use release is a good UX for the Verevon cross-plane provenance and screening envelope; pair it with deny-by-default (QM still fails open when the screener is unavailable, see tool_result_failed_open at orchestrator.ts:3857).
notes: Quality 4: fail-safe by construction (release only by approval, one time) and tested (test/screening-release.test.ts); depends on a classifier that can fail open. Known weakness: effectful paths can proceed as unscreened on screener errors (docs/deploy-directory.md says enforce fails closed; code does not). Verevon plan already treats this as a negative test.

name: Credential broker: calls with a secret the agent never sees
what: For broker-delivery credentials the sandbox sends only a credential slug, method and URL to core; core attaches the secret, enforces the pinned host, https only, method and path allowlists, strips unsafe headers, adds an optional actor-attestation header, caps the response and audits every use.
how: brokerCredentialCall() checks entitlement from capability claims, rejects reserved x-qm-actor, requires https and host match (exact host when actor attestation is on), checks allowedMethods and allowedPathPrefixes (decoded up to 4 times to catch ..), uses fetch redirect:manual, caps responses at 5 MB and records credential.broker.use/denied/error audit and usage events. Keychain credentials have kinds env, file and broker.
verevonRelevance: The strongest answer in the corpus to 'agent PC with real accounts': a proxy-style secret broker with per-credential host/method/path pinning and per-person attestation; Verevon should expose Control/Integration-core credentials to Space agents the same way (short-lived, action-bound, never in the sandbox).
notes: Quality 5: strongest secret design among the peers read: https, host and path binding, redirect refusal, size cap, audit, tested in test/credential-broker.test.ts; plaintext escape hatches still exist elsewhere. SPEC concedes env and file delivery remain escape hatches (docs/SPEC.md:23); SECURITY.md:146-155 notes purposes are advisory only. Uniqueness reviewed: the underlying technique is general engineering; it is distinctive mainly in how it is applied to agents in shared rooms.

name: Cross-person credential asks routed as approval cards
what: When a command needs a credential owned by someone else, the agent files an ask with a one-sentence purpose; the owner gets a card where the conversation is happening (or in their DM) and approves once, as a standing grant, or denies. Nothing said in chat counts as approval.
how: KeychainAsk and KeychainGrant (mode once|standing, audienceScopeId, expiry, revokedAt, usedAt); approvalCardDestination() sends the card to the requesting thread, a cron's destination, inline web, or falls back to the owner's DM; decide(id, actor, once|standing|deny). request-access skill documents the agent side.
verevonRelevance: Fits the Verevon Space credential grant broker (S3.4): grants are bound to the room audience and owner-approved, with the card placed where the work happens.
notes: Quality 4: asks, grants and cards are durable and tested (test/keychain-ask.test.ts, test/keychain-approval-card.test.ts); depends on Slack or web cards reaching the owner. Grants carry a purpose string that core does not enforce (SECURITY.md:151).

name: Secret drop: one-time web form so secrets bypass chat and model
what: When a secret is needed, the platform mints a single-use link to a form owned by the platform; the human types the value there, so it never passes through the conversation or the model context.
how: SecretDropStore.mint() returns a long random dropId (two UUIDs), peek() previews, redeem() atomically takes the record; records expire after 7 days and carry service, fields, purpose, audience scope and destination; the page is a platform-styled HTML route.
verevonRelevance: A small, copyable pattern for Verevon credential and PII capture inside a Space without leaking values into thread history or ZDR-sensitive stores.
notes: Quality 4: small, atomic and expiring (test/secret-drop.test.ts); a bearer URL for seven days is the main exposure.

name: Interactive login by agent-driven device flow, saved as keychain files
what: The agent can log a CLI in (aws sso, gh, glab, gcloud) by running the device-code flow in a temp home, relaying the URL and code to the human, and saving the resulting config files to the person's keychain; later commands stage those files into a private home per command.
how: interactive-login skill + save-login.mjs script; resident credential path lists (.aws, .config/gh, .config/gcloud, .ssh, .netrc) and ephemeral staging under /tmp/agent-creds; refreshed tokens written back at command end; displaced-path pruning keeps credentials out of home snapshots.
verevonRelevance: A pragmatic human-to-agent handoff for 'give the agent a logged-in computer' that Verevon can model as a Quarry/Integration grant flow instead of file capture.
notes: Quality 3: works for CLI device flows and is documented, but it deliberately stores tokens on disk where a prompt-injected agent could read them (SPEC credentials note). SPEC lists credential capture as a band-aid-prone area (qm#2137 on browser-profile sweeps); files are plaintext while in use.

name: Per-turn capability tokens bind the sandbox to scope, run and lease
what: Everything the agent's computer calls back into core with carries a signed token scoped to one audience (agent API, credential broker, egress proxy, blob transfer, secret drop, control plane), the scope, actor, roster, egress policy and the exact run attempt and lease.
how: mintCapabilityToken(claims, secret) signs JSON with HMAC; CapabilityClaims include aud, scopeId, actorId, members, egress, memory read/write scopes, credentials, runId, runAttempt, runLeaseToken; verifyCapabilityToken() validates every field; optional deflate-raw compression above 4096 bytes; sandbox tokens default to 48h (SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_TTL_HOURS), exp 0 only for four dedicated audiences.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already uses short-lived Ed25519 decisions bound to effect; QM adds run-lease binding and per-audience tokens for the sandbox, which suits Space leases (S3.2). Avoid copying the long 48h default.
notes: Quality 4: typed, validated and secret-isolated (test/capability-token.test.ts, test/capability-secret-isolation.test.ts); 48-hour bearer lifetime and plaintext use inside the sandbox are known limits. Revocation relies on scope checks and expiry; non-expiring bearer tokens are exposure risks (docs/capability-tokens.md).

name: Open sharing posture: bounded cross-context reads with audit and disposable owner computers
what: An org can let a person's own personal files, skills and memory be used in a shared room they belong to (and the reverse in their DM), with caps, current-membership rechecks and an audit trail; credentials are used only in a separate disposable computer.
how: sharingSourcesForTurn() returns eligible source scopes only for live trusted human (or live ambient) turns on Open posture, at most 25 shared scopes, 100 candidate sessions, 200 files; carriedFileHandles() maps files to shared/open-<scope>/ handles; every read is audited as sharing.cross_context_read; composePosture lets Isolated win at org, personal, room and source-room.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a worked model for 'bring my personal context into a Space' with explicit caps and audit; Verevon must keep owner-plane ACLs and never widen them (Space membership never widens an ACL).
notes: Quality 3: tight caps, audit and an explicit isolated override (test/sharing-posture.test.ts, test/sharing-context-e2e.test.ts), yet SECURITY.md concedes it relies on model discretion after authorization. SECURITY.md:137 states Open sharing relies on model discretion after authorization; it is a disclosure tradeoff, not a filter.

name: Agent computer as an independent, agent-managed resource
what: A sandbox is a recorded resource with an owning scope, provider, backing identity and lifecycle; the agent itself can list providers, create blank computers, set a default, check status, restart or retire them. Execution without a selected default fails explicitly instead of provisioning one silently.
how: SandboxResources records resources and an explicit per-scope default; the sandbox tool exposes list, create, set_default, status, restart, retire; execute takes an optional sandbox_id; NoDefaultSandboxError tells the agent to list, create and set a default; retirement requires clearing the default and stopping jobs; in Open posture the acting person's personal sandboxes and Open shared sandboxes can be targeted with both policies applied and egress narrowed to satisfy both.
verevonRelevance: Fits the Verevon plan (S3.2) for a Space-scoped lease with a typed profile; the explicit resource record plus 'no default means no execution' avoids silent fallbacks and gives the UI something to list.
notes: Quality 4: the agent can manage computers, with explicit defaults and refusals (test/sandbox-resources.test.ts); the capability is new and the matrix of backends is large. Introduced by commit 791a9c5b (2026-09-09), so it postdates the 2026-08-13 Verevon baseline. The old routing table is retained only as upgrade input.

name: Backend capability profile with explicit refusal (no substitute computer)
what: Each computer backend declares what it can do (persistence kind, process sessions, parks on teardown, egress enforcement none/ip_port/domain); calls the backend cannot honor fail with a named capability error, and an unavailable selected backend is refused rather than replaced by another provider.
how: AgentComputerProfile {backend, writablePersistence, processSessions, parksOnTeardown, egressEnforcement, spec}; Sandbox interface has optional methods; the router's requireCap() throws CapabilityUnsupportedError and reports it once to the error log; backendFor() throws 'refusing to use a substitute computer'; effectiveEgressEnforcement() reports none unless core signing and API base are configured.
verevonRelevance: Exactly the Verevon baseline pattern 'substrate capability profile that fails closed on downgrade'; the concrete shape (profile + optional methods + typed refusal) is directly reusable for Model Plane sandboxes and for Quarry-backed browser sessions.
notes: Quality 4: honest profile and no silent substitution (test/agent-computer-profile.test.ts); egress enforcement is conditional per backend. docs/SPEC.md:112-117 records provider drift as a lens: adding providers that subtly deviate from the contract has happened several times (parksOnTeardown was added to remove a Modal special case, qm#1748).

name: Ten computer backends behind one contract (and the cost of that choice)
what: The agent computer can be Fly Sprites, smolmachines, E2B, Modal, Porter, Agent37, Superserve, DigitalOcean Managed Agents, AWS Lambda microVMs or local Docker; an org picks the substrate and the agent sees the same machine.
how: SandboxBackendName union and one implementation file per provider (about 11.8K lines under src/sandbox, largest modal-sandbox 968 and sprites-sandbox 718); shared helpers for exec files, process polling, ro layers and snapshots; a guest agent for AWS microVMs exposes only /health, /exec, /write and /read over HTTP; fakes for every provider live in test/support. The same guest daemon (aws/microvm-agent/agent.mjs) is copied into the local Docker sandbox image and used for published apps on AWS. The Fly Machines sandbox backend was retired, SANDBOX_SECONDARY_BACKEND, the sandbox_routing table and SANDBOX_RESOURCES_ENABLED are retired, and the CLI config schema names only local, sprites, aws, agent37 and superserve (others are selected through core env).
verevonRelevance: Verevon should not copy the breadth: SPEC itself lists ten providers as config-matrix expansion. Copy the contract and the fake-provider test harness; pick two substrates.
notes: Quality 3 because the maintainers flag it as a maintenance burden (config-matrix and provider-drift lenses). Uniqueness reviewed: the underlying technique is general engineering; it is distinctive mainly in how it is applied to agents in shared rooms.

name: Agent home persistence: provider checkpoints plus portable S3 tar, with refuse-to-adopt-blank rules
what: A person's or room's computer keeps its installed tools and files across sleeps and rebuilds through provider-native checkpoints where available and a throttled tar of the home in object storage elsewhere; incomplete or expired restores stop with an explicit error rather than silently starting from an empty home.
how: snapshotDue() throttles by interval and home-dirty flag; HOME_SNAPSHOT_PRUNE excludes caches and credential staging; multipart S3 upload with a 2 GiB cap; Modal native directory checkpoints, E2B createSnapshot, Sprites checkpoints, DO checkpoints; initialization recorded pending in a durable map before create so a lost response cannot skip hydration; failed hydration kills the replacement instead of adopting it; checkpoint renewal sweep before provider retention expires.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Model Plane snapshot registry is currently in memory (baseline section 7); QM's pending-marker-before-create and 'never replace a saved home with blank' rules are the durable-state invariants to adopt for Space workspaces.
notes: Quality 4: careful about lost responses and blank restores (test/home-snapshot.test.ts); RAM and processes are never preserved and artifacts have no expiry. SECURITY.md:174-177: file artifacts and deduplicated bytes have no expiry or reclamation. Processes and RAM are never preserved.

name: Layered workspace mounts: org read-only, team read-only, scope read-write
what: The agent's filesystem is layered: a read-only org layer mounted at global/, read-only team layers at team-<id>/, and the active scope's own writable layer at the root.
how: resolve() builds WorkspaceLayer[] with mode ro/rw and mountPath; materializeRoLayers() tars all read-only layer files, fingerprints them with sha256 over path+content and only rewrites the sandbox copy when the manifest hash differs.
verevonRelevance: Matches the Verevon S3.3 plan (org read-only layer, Space RW volume, per-run overlay) with a cheap fingerprint-based sync; Verevon should back the layers with Data Plane object references, not local scope directories.
notes: Quality 3: simple fingerprinted tar of read-only layers, covered through resolution tests; layer count and size limits not examined.

name: Forced egress through an authorizing proxy, with provider-level network enforcement
what: All sandbox traffic is forced through an Envoy forward proxy that asks a local decision service whether this turn's token allows the host; private ranges, cloud metadata and loopback are always blocked, DNS answers are pinned, and the proxy fails closed. Where a provider supports it, the sandbox network is locked so only the proxy host is reachable.
how: Envoy listener runs a Lua filter that calls egress-authz /check with the Proxy-Authorization capability token (aud egress-proxy); the service evaluates the token's EgressPolicy (allow list, deny list, privateNetworkAllowedHosts, denyPrivateNetworks), resolves DNS, rejects blocked subnets and returns an x-egress-upstream-address so Envoy dials the checked IP; admin interface is a 0600 unix socket; audit records are relayed to core in batches (cap 5,000). Provider-level outbound rules limited to the proxy host are set for E2B, Modal, DigitalOcean, Sprites, smolmachines and Porter (see the typed egress capability record); backends without that capability (AWS, local Docker, Agent37, Superserve) report none and boot only warns about fail-open.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon baseline rates Quarry-v2 SSRF handling at or above QM; the transferable idea is binding the egress decision to the per-turn capability token so a shared room's audience floor reaches the network layer.
notes: Quality 4: authz, DNS pinning and audit are tested (test/egress-authz.test.ts, test/egress-proxy-config.test.ts); enforcement is conditional on the backend and runtime-deployment egress is not built (SECURITY.md). SECURITY.md:167-169: enforcement is conditional on backend network rules and deployment-runtime egress enforcement is not built. Browser traffic exits through the browser provider, not this proxy (SECURITY.md:142-145). Corrected in the verification pass: six backends can lock to the proxy host, not only E2B and Modal.

name: Scoped notebook memory with sensitivity classes and provenance
what: Each scope has a revisioned notebook of records; every record has a sensitivity class (ordinary, unknown, sensitive, restricted) and source references, and a reader only sees a record if they are entitled to every source it came from.
how: Postgres memory_revisions stores authoritative records JSON per scope with compare-and-swap revisions; extraction classifies each batch; consolidation edits records by stable id under a revision check and only mixes records of identical sensitivity and provenance; disclosedMemory() applies one disclosure view to recall, search, tools and APIs; whole-notebook rewrites inherit the combined restrictions and cannot declassify.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space memory scope yet (baseline section 7); QM's record-level provenance and 'cross-room personal facts keep their source' rules are the model for Space memory that never auto-copies room facts into personal memory.
notes: Quality 4: classification, provenance and CAS revisions are tested (test/memory-records.test.ts, test/memory-disclosure.test.ts); classification is a model estimate and the notebook is whole-file loaded. Introduced by commit 58a9dc63 (2026-09-29). Classification is a model estimate, not proof (docs/memory-records.md:23-28). SPEC:196-199 notes per-fact provenance boilerplate still costs tokens.

name: Durable context boundary when a room's audience changes
what: When the people in a conversation change, earlier model history, summaries, native harness state, retries, approvals and tape rows from before the change cannot re-enter the next turn; later turns keep post-change context normally.
how: A durable session checkpoint records an audience identity hash and a replay cutoff; an actual audience change advances the cutoff; agent conversation APIs and subagent reads honor it; human transcripts and admin audit stay intact; project conversations keep member-inherits-history.
verevonRelevance: A Space whose membership changes needs exactly this next-turn isolation; Verevon's per-entry audience revision plan should add an explicit cutoff checkpoint.
notes: Quality 4: durable cutoff with tests (test/memory-context-boundary.test.ts); mostly documented in docs/memory-records.md rather than traced end to end here. Documented in docs/memory-records.md; implementation was not traced end to end. It is next-turn isolation only, not retroactive deletion.

name: Scope-routed external memory providers (MCP) with failure policy
what: Memory can be recalled from and written to external systems per scope kind or exact scope, with separate read and write OAuth client credentials, capture policies (off, explicit, automatic) and fail-open or fail-closed per route.
how: MEMORY_PROVIDER_CONFIG defines providers (type mcp or memorable) and routes (provider, scopes, capture, manage, label, failOpen); QM keeps deciding readable and writable scopes and passes acting_user; explicit writes always fail visibly; procedural memory (Memorable) records procedures not facts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has Data Plane knowledge and Dreaming memory; the useful idea is routing by scope kind with an explicit acting_user argument so the owner plane keeps authorization.

name: Skills as scope-owned, governed packages with git-pack import and explicit loading
what: Skills are SKILL.md packages owned by a scope and shareable by grant; an admin can register a pinned git repository as a pack, review a catalog with eligibility reasons and import skills org-wide; the agent loads a skill through a tool that returns the body without waking a sandbox.

Phase A is org scope only and pinned refs; tracked sync is Phase B. Skills carried in Open sharing must pass screening before inclusion (SECURITY.md:99-101). Corrected in the verification pass: docs/skill-registry.md still says tracked sync is a later phase, but createSkillSyncEngine is implemented and wired (src/skills/skill-sync-engine.ts, src/wiring.ts:2586): tracked packs are reconciled when the upstream head moves and manual packs only get an updateAvailable flag, on a leader-lease tick (SKILL_SYNC_POLL_MS, default 300 s).

name: Goals with an independent governor; the agent cannot end its own goal
what: A person can give the agent a long-running goal; the harness keeps answering an attempt to stop with a completion-audit prompt, and a fresh-context judge model, not the working agent, decides continue, complete, step back or pause. Only a human stop pauses a goal and only a person's own message resumes it.
how: GoalRecord {objective, status, floor, capTokens, tokensUsed, activeMs, governor, pauseReason}; governor runs every 3 continuation rounds or 30 minutes of work and when completion is requested; verdicts continue|complete|step_back|pause with pause only right after a step back on the same blocker; budgets (min turns/ms/tokens/usd floor and token cap) are rails, never the goal; goal enforcement is wrapped around every harness in harness-router.
verevonRelevance: A strong control for Space agents that run for hours (Chief/Core routing, scheduled work): the separation between the working agent and an independent stop/complete judge, with human-only resume, is a ready template.
notes: Quality 4: governor design is carefully argued and tested (test/goal.test.ts, test/harness-router-goal.test.ts); the subsystem changed weekly in September and October, so it is still moving. Added after the 2026-08-13 baseline (commits 9143874b, dc93931b, 2026-09 to 2026-10). The doc comment in goal.ts is the clearest statement of the rules.

name: Ambient participation by a cheap observer with standing orders
what: In a channel the agent can decide whether to chime in on messages that did not address it: a thin judge model sees a batch of overheard messages, the assistant's identity and the room's standing orders, defaults to silence, and only spawns a full worker when someone is addressing the assistant, clearly needs something it can provide, or a standing order matches.
how: judgeAmbientBatch() renders AMBIENT_JUDGE_SYSTEM + identity + standing orders + earlier context (marked do-not-act) + new messages, parses {act, reason, asked_by}; on act it calls spawnWorker(batch, decision); scheduled check-ins can fire with no new messages; per-room ambientEnabled and policy history live in channel_policy tables; judgments are stored and viewable in admin.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's roadmap has ambient web presence only as an opt-in later phase; this is a concrete, cheap two-tier design (observer judge plus worker) with silence as default.
notes: Quality 4: cheap judge plus standing orders, stored and viewable (test/ambient-judge.test.ts); judge quality is model-dependent and is a cost per message batch. SECURITY.md:193-195: the ambient judge's model call does not yet use the ModelGateway and its internal-only check is weaker than addressed turns.

name: Per-room standing orders, bot ledger and revision history
what: Each channel can hold a proactivity policy (standing orders), a ledger telling the agent how to treat other bots in the room (ignore, rollup of N hours, action, treat as user), an ambient on/off switch, and a revision history with compare-and-swap edits.
how: ChannelPolicy {container, orders, bots, ambientEnabled}; BOT_MODES ignore|rollup|action|user with rollupHours; parseBotLedger caps 200 bots; set() takes expectedOrders and appends channel_policy_history rows including session id.
verevonRelevance: A small, directly adoptable per-Space settings object for agent behavior toward other agents and bots; Verevon has Space instructions but no bot/agent-interaction ledger or versioning (baseline section 7: no versioning).
notes: Quality 4: versioned policy with optimistic checks (test/surface-cache-ambient.test.ts); small and clear.

name: Responsive spine: coordinator turn dispatches to subagents and ends fast
what: For people with the flag, the front-line agent in Slack or web cannot run commands itself; it acknowledges, delegates the substantial work to child sessions, ends its turn quickly and is woken with a durable completion notice to report the result.
how: responsive_spine and persistent_subagents are per-person feature flags; spine turns get surfaceTools and an addressed wake text, record the first text block as an acknowledgement, and are re-engaged by completion wakes; coordinator turns disable command execution, background tools, credential execution and provider-native delegation.
verevonRelevance: Solves the 'room goes silent while the agent works' problem that a Space with polling already has; adoptable as: a fast front agent plus Model Plane runs with wake-on-completion.
notes: Quality 3: feature-flagged and young (test/surface-spine-routing.test.ts); behaviour assembled from docs and orchestrator paths, not fully traced. Feature-flagged and off by default; behavior assembled from docs and orchestrator hits, not a full trace. Introduced after the baseline.

name: Persistent subagents with durable mailbox and tree caps
what: A delegated task runs as a child session with its own transcript, computer (or none), attributed messages and a mutable parent; children inherit scope and audience; the session tree admits a capped number of pending or running runs (50 in code); parents get a deduplicated completion notice that survives restarts.
how: subagents tool open/send_message/wait/followup_task; session mailbox stored in a durable map with putIfAbsent and consumed-after-persist semantics; request keys make open idempotent; noComputer removes shell, files and browser; terminal receipts live in the run store and a paginated sweep retries returns; interrupt:true aborts child work; messages are screened and quarantine-recoverable.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Space has no agent-to-agent delegation path (baseline section 7, UI-2c); QM shows the durable shape: child session, inbox, wake receipts, tree cap and inherited audience.
notes: Quality 4: durable mailbox with idempotent open and tree caps (test/session-syscalls.test.ts, test/subagent-parity.test.ts); flagged and recent. Doc drift: docs/persistent-subagent-sessions.md:9 says ten pending or running runs per tree, but code sets SUBAGENT_TREE_RUN_CAP = 50 (src/sessions/session-syscalls.ts:102, raised in commit 93b2c434 on 2026-10-09). Treat code as truth.

name: Swarms: durable agent pools with ordered messages and a shared board computer
what: An agent can spawn a pool of worker sessions that coordinate through a durable per-swarm message log with monotonic sequence numbers, audience lists, wake-on-message and a shared 'forum' computer; the pool has finite lifetime and notification budgets.
how: POST /v1/swarm spawn/send/context/control with required requestId idempotency; a durable outbox reserves members, provisions computers (3 attempts, 10 s per attempt, 30 s per phase), creates sessions and queues initial turns; each worker gets a blank private computer and the swarm gets one board computer; agent operations require a token bound to session, run attempt and lease and recheck the lease inside the DB transaction; workers never inherit the root's approval grants.
verevonRelevance: A reference for multi-agent coordination inside a Space (S4 work cockpit) with idempotent reservations, ordered messaging and lease-checked writes.
notes: Quality 3: ambitious and tested (test/swarms.test.ts, test/swarm-api.test.ts) but young, flagged and dependent on a swarm-capable provider. Feature-flagged per person; added after the baseline. Quality 3: sophisticated but young, and requires Postgres plus a swarm-capable sandbox provider.

name: Agent reach: posting is bounded by the acting human's membership
what: When the agent messages another person, channel or group DM it resolves the target through the directory, requires the acting human (not the bot) to be able to see a private room, caps group DMs at 8 people, caps cross-conversation posts at 5 per turn and queues the post through the durable delivery store.
how: resolveReachTarget() resolves recipient|channel|participants, returns typed errors (not_a_member, identity_unverified, ambiguous_recipient, group_too_large) and builds a Destination with audienceScopeId; SpineState.crossConversationPosts >= 5 refuses; hand-off skill tells the agent to DM with the full request and never post it in a channel.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Verevon agents that post into Spaces or notify people: authority for 'who may the agent reach' derives from the human principal and Control rosters, with hard per-turn limits.
notes: Quality 4: typed refusals and caps, tested in test/reach.test.ts and test/scope-reach.test.ts; the five-post cap is a blunt limit.

name: Agent tasks list and reaction-based progress acknowledgement
what: The agent keeps a durable task list per run and the Slack surface mirrors it as a task card and as an emoji reaction on the requester's message that changes as work progresses; web shows work duration, subagent cards and a goal indicator.
how: TaskStore (pending, in_progress, completed, skipped, failed) with task events; createTaskAcknowledgements() applies reaction swaps under a keyed queue and leader lease with recovery from run and delivery state; ack emoji can be picked by the helper model; waitRun emits onTasks/onGoal when snapshots change.
verevonRelevance: A cheap, always-visible 'agent is working' signal for Space rooms that does not require a new transport; the durable task list is also what a Work cockpit tab can project.
notes: Quality 3: durable tasks and ack swaps under a lease (test/task-store.test.ts, test/slack-task-ack.test.ts); SPEC lists completion ownership as a band-aid. Slack task cards are opt-in (commit 82342138).

name: Tool-result hygiene: head-and-tail cap with narrow-refetch guidance
what: Large tool outputs are capped at 100k characters keeping the head and the last 10k characters with a notice telling the model to refetch narrower or redirect to a file, so conclusions and errors at the end are not lost.
how: capResultText() keeps headSlice and tailSlice around a fixed notice; MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS 100000, TRUNCATED_TAIL_CHARS 10000; pressure warnings added when IO stall is high.
verevonRelevance: Listed as a P0/P1 item in the Verevon adoption plan with a stale pointer (pi-tools.ts:82-94); the implementation is now here and is a 15-line port.
notes: Quality 4: exact, small and effective; the numeric caps are fixed constants.

name: Client-executed tools: the caller supplies tools the agent can call mid-turn
what: A turn request can declare tools the client will execute (name, description, JSON schema, timeout); the agent calls them like any tool and the run waits for a client result delivered as a durable signal.
how: ClientToolDeclaration and ClientToolResult in the turn request; RunSignalKind includes client_result; waitForClientResult() blocks until the result arrives; externalTools() proxy denies all other tools for guest or external-audience turns.
verevonRelevance: A path for local desktop or browser capabilities (user's own screen, files, a signed-in browser) to be offered to a Space agent without moving credentials; fits a future Verevon desktop shell.
notes: Quality 3: typed round trip over the run-signal store; only one use shape and little documentation. Only the data model and signal path were read; no first-party client implementation was found in plugins/web-ui during this pass.

name: Admin operations as an agent tool over existing handlers
what: An org admin can ask the agent to inspect or change scope configuration (read config, update one nonsecret resource, read credential usage, read or replace notebooks, list sessions) through a typed operation table that calls the same authenticated admin handlers.
how: adminOperations is a table of operations with typebox schemas (additionalProperties false), HTTP method and path; authority is rechecked per call and audited; secret-bearing setters stay on the self-API; large transcript reads are paginated.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Verevon 'ask the agent to configure the Space' flows; keep human-only walls and do not expose grant, role or approval changes (see human-only authority walls).
notes: Quality 3: thin table over existing handlers with authority rechecked (test/admin-tool.test.ts); SPEC records an earlier over-engineered attempt that was cut. SPEC cites an earlier 43-file attempt as over-engineering; the current table is small.

name: Per-person and per-org durable feature flags for preview features
what: Previews (swarms, persistent subagents, responsive spine, inbox loops, team scopes, app annotations, external app sharing) are enabled per person scope (personal:<id>) or org-wide through an admin table, and routes and tool catalogs omit the feature when off.
how: FeatureFlagStore over a DurableMap with enabledScopes; enabled(name, scope) is true if org scope or the scope is listed; orchestration and /v1/apis check flags per actor even in shared conversations.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already needs deny-by-default per-org policy rows; per-person scope targeting for staged rollout of Space features is a cheap complement.
notes: Quality 3: simple durable store (test/feature-flags.test.ts); per-person flags also gate tool availability, which complicates reasoning. Nine flags as of this HEAD; the flag set is part of the config-matrix burden.

name: Scheduled agent work with deterministic fire keys and one fresh thread per fire
what: A scope can own recurring or one-shot agent jobs; each fire gets a deterministic key, runs in its own fresh thread, records a fire log (running, ok, silent, deferred, failed, refused), leaves a note for the next fire and can deliver to a destination.
how: createPgBossCronQueue() queues fire jobs; fireEnabled() builds cronFireThreadRef(cronId, fireKey), begins an exclusive fire (beginExclusive rejects a second running fire inside staleRunningMs), runs runTrigger() with the cron authority, records deferred/failed/refused outcomes; sweepStranded() fails fires stuck running; scheduled fires defer 30 s when the session is busy (up to 10 minutes late); one-shot crons disable themselves; continuity is through published Files and a per-cron note.
verevonRelevance: The baseline already tells Verevon to carry the fire-key and slot-claim invariant into the existing Model cron and Temporal paths; the per-fire thread plus next-fire note is a cheap continuity design to copy.
notes: Quality 4: deterministic keys, exclusive fires and a fire log (test/cron-scheduler.test.ts, test/cron-queue.test.ts, test/postgres-cron-fires.test.ts); one of the better scheduled-agent designs read. Per-second tick job was removed in qm#2007 (git b528b8ff) because idle scheduling caused DB writes; mutation hooks and periodic repair on the lease holder replace it.

name: Unattended runs re-authorize at every fire and run as owner, floor or shared
what: A schedule never keeps acting after its owner or audience loses access: every fire re-checks that the acting person is still internal and still a member of the room, and runs as the owner, as the least-privileged common member, or as the owner with shared-scope membership.
how: TriggerSpec.runAs owner|scopeFloor|scopeShared; runTrigger() refreshes identity, loads current scope members, skips the fire with an explanatory note when membership is gone (MEMBERSHIP_SKIP_NOTE) or the owner is no longer internal; scopeFloor builds the audience from current members; scopeShared also requires current Open membership for owner resources; unattended credential grants require a live turn by the owner, a personal-scope cron running as owner and a current org admin.
verevonRelevance: This is the fresh-authorization-at-fire pattern the Verevon plan lists as P1 for Space cron; the three runAs modes give a vocabulary for 'who is the agent acting as' in unattended Space work.
notes: Quality 4: re-authorization at every fire is enforced and tested (test/run-trigger.test.ts, test/cron-credential-resumption.test.ts). SPEC:27: unattended work is considered more of a prompt-injection risk, so credentials need explicit grants.

name: Recipient consent and no-escalation rule for triggers
what: A standing automation that delivers to another person's DM only runs after that recipient accepts; creating an automation owned by someone else requires that person's consent.
how: consentRequiredRecipient(), recipientConsentSatisfied(), decideRecipientConsent() and assertNoEscalation() in trigger-store; crons set recipientConsentRequired for recurring schedules; /v1/triggers/:id/consent routes; a consent notice is delivered to the recipient.
verevonRelevance: Prevents a Space agent from turning one member's standing orders into unsolicited notifications for another member; adopt as a rule for agent-scheduled notifications.
notes: Quality 4: small explicit consent state machine (test/trigger-consent.test.ts, test/trigger-store.test.ts).

name: Poll surfaces may answer 'no update' and stay silent
what: Unattended polling runs (cron, webhook, monitor) can end with a sentinel reply such as [no-update] and nothing is delivered, so schedules do not spam rooms when nothing changed.
how: POLL_SURFACES = cron|webhook|monitor; SILENT_POLL_MARKERS [no-update], no_reply, [silent]; isSilentPollReply() inspects the final non-empty line; finish_silently is a no-effect turn ender.
verevonRelevance: A small contract that keeps proactive Space agents tolerable; make the silent outcome explicit in the run result schema rather than a text sentinel.
notes: Quality 3: marker-based silence is simple and tested (test/poll-fire-silence.test.ts) but is text matching on model output. The sentinel is text-matched, which docs/SPEC.md:145-153 would classify under the regex/band-aid lenses.

name: Durable watches on background processes with cursor, pattern and expiry
what: The agent can watch a long-running process; the watch survives restarts, tracks an output cursor, optionally matches a literal pattern, expires, and wakes the conversation with output or exit.
how: MonitorBroker.watch(processId, {instructions, pattern, sinceCursor}) returns armed or already-completed results with a 4 KB output tail; MonitorStore holds cursor, lastFiredAt, expiresAt and records errors; patterns must be literal alternatives (no regex metacharacters, 256 chars); defunct monitors are deleted after 7 days; ProcessRegistry and reaper reconcile process records with the sandbox.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plan S4.3 wants a general watch primitive; QM shows the minimal durable record (cursor, heartbeat, expiry, destination, cancel) and the literal-pattern restriction that avoids regex DoS.
notes: Quality 4: durable cursors and expiry (test/monitor-broker.test.ts, test/monitor-store.test.ts); scope limited to background processes. Only process watches exist; kinds beyond a process id were not found.

name: Loops: durable work queues with a ship gate and a trust ladder
what: A Loop turns a stream of events (schedule, signed webhook, Slack events, Gmail push) into queued items the agent works through; every outward action has a declared gate, held for human review by default, and a person can graduate a specific action to automatic. A governor quarantines or throttles a loop that keeps failing or whose outputs are mostly returned.
how: decideShip() returns auto (policy or grant), hold or undeclared; buildShipGrant() makes a content-hash id from loop, policy version, action and label and is refused when the org disables standing grants; evaluateGovernor() derives health healthy|degraded|failing|quarantined from consecutive failed fires (3), return rate (over 50 percent after 4 decisions) and undeclared ship actions, with throttle and ping actions; ledger and outputs persist per item.
verevonRelevance: The most distinctive human-in-the-loop idea in QM: autonomy earned by track record per action, with automatic throttling when humans keep rejecting outputs. A Space could expose 'graduate this action' on approval cards.
notes: Quality 4: ship gate and governor are well specified and tested (test/loop-ship-gate.test.ts, test/loop-governor.test.ts); the subsystem is flagged and SPEC says it should have reused crons. Flagged (inbox_loops) and added after the baseline (commit a921fb0c). SPEC:44 says the loops subsystem should have reused crons and 'built its own little empire'; treat as an idea source, not a structure to copy.

name: Event ingestion acknowledged only after durable receipt
what: External events (signed webhook, Slack Events, Gmail Pub/Sub) are acknowledged to the sender only after they are durably stored; duplicates reuse the same item; paused loops keep received work; Gmail uses history cursors with ten-minute reconciliation and daily watch renewal.
how: Signed webhook body HMAC-SHA256 in X-Signature, 64 KB cap, 202 on receipt, 401 bad signature, 404 unknown; Slack events deduplicate by event id; Gmail push verifies Google signature, issuer, audience and service-account email and only advances the cursor after items are durably imported; completed receipt metadata kept 30 days.
verevonRelevance: The ack-after-durable discipline is the right contract for Space inbound webhooks and Channel Plane adapters; Verevon already needs it for integration-corev2 provider events.
notes: Quality 4: ack-after-durable ordering is explicit (test/loop-ingress.test.ts, test/loop-ingress-pg.test.ts); documented as flagged. Slack receipt recovery covers only events QM already persisted; there is no history reconciliation for Slack (docs/loop-ingestion.md:13).

name: Suggested activities generated by a managed per-person cron
what: Each user gets personalized starter prompts that are refreshed in the background (nightly, every four hours for busy users, paused after 30 days of inactivity) by an ordinary personal cron using the user's own context.
how: Opening a new personal chat enrolls the user in a cron named 'Refresh my suggested activities'; the task in src/suggestions/activities.ts asks for three validated activity objects with no delivery destination; cadence is reevaluated hourly; owner can pause, edit or delete the cron.
verevonRelevance: Shows how to ship a proactive product feature on top of the existing cron machinery with no new scheduler; a Space 'what should we do next' card could be built the same way.
notes: Quality 3: reuses the cron machinery (test/suggested-activities.test.ts); product value is modest. Dogfoods crons, so all authorization and fire-log behavior applies.

name: External (guest) audience turns: restricted namespace, deny-by-default tools, private continuation
what: In a Slack workspace shared with outsiders every non-DM conversation is treated as an external audience: the agent gets its own restricted computer and conversation namespace, no personal or org memory, files, skills, keychain or MCP tools, only an allowlisted set of service credentials, and can hand the person's request into their private DM instead of answering in the channel.
how: externalSlack accounts configured with companyDomains, companyTeamIds and serviceCredentials; resolve(external=true) drops org and team layers, souls and granted handles; externalTools() is a deny-by-default Proxy that allows only attach, history and a few helpers and throws a message pointing to [[continue-private: task]]; private continuation rechecks the employee against current policy, opens the DM and queues a normal personal-context turn; policy changes start a fresh namespace.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's baseline finds guests and external members absent (section 2); this is the most concrete worked design for agent behavior with guests: a restricted namespace plus private continuation, not a widened room.
notes: Quality 4: deny-by-default proxy and private continuation are tested (test/external-slack-core.test.ts, test/external-slack-policy.test.ts); limited to Slack guests. Added after the baseline (commit cc95b9ef). Deployment-level config only, no admin UI. SECURITY.md:24-33 still says guests are outside the supported interaction boundary except this opt-in.

name: Per-session serialized durable run queue in Postgres
what: Every agent turn is a durable run row; runs for one session execute strictly in order and at most one runs at a time, across any number of workers and instances; duplicate submissions are deduplicated by an idempotency key.
how: runs table with unique partial index idx_runs_one_running_per_session WHERE status='running'; claim() is one UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) that refuses a run if any sibling in the session is running, earlier in (created_at, seq) order, or backing off; enqueue() is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING with pg_notify('qm_run_available'); lease token and expiry are on the row.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon plan says port QM's invariants and tests, not its queue (Temporal/NATS exist). The invariants to assert on the Model Plane run model: one running run per session, FIFO within a session, token-fenced completion, dedup key.
notes: Quality 4: unique-index plus SKIP LOCKED claim is sound and tested (test/run-store.test.ts); SPEC says retry and wakeup code hand-rolls what pg-boss offers. SPEC:81-83 calls custom retry and wakeup machinery hand-rolling versus pg-boss (qm#1005, #1255); still on main.

name: Worker lease heartbeat, lease-loss self-cancel, crash-loop parking
what: A worker renews its run lease on a timer; if it fails to renew three consecutive times it aborts the in-process turn so a replacement can safely take over; runs that are claimed too many times without completing are parked as suspected crash loops; a leader-elected reaper requeues expired leases.
how: processRun() starts a heartbeat at ttl/3, counts consecutive lost beats (LEASE_LOST_CONSECUTIVE 3) and aborts; fail() applies errorAttempts/maxAttempts; retire() parks when attempts >= maxClaims; reapExpired runs under a Postgres advisory-lock leader lease (runs:reaper); complete() is token-fenced.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Temporal activity heartbeats on the Model Plane; the explicit 'lost lease cancels local work' and crash-loop park rules are worth encoding as acceptance tests.
notes: Quality 4: lease heartbeat, self-cancel and crash-loop parking are tested (test/worker-reaper.test.ts, test/run-stale.test.ts); unremarkable but correct.

name: Session writer lease with typed holders and progress-based keepalive
what: Only one actor at a time may append to a conversation's log (a turn, a compaction, a fork or a backfill); the lease is renewed only while the turn shows progress and the turn is aborted if it stalls.
how: LeaseHolder 'turn'|'compaction'|'fork'|'backfill'; acquireLeaseWithin() waits for a holder predicate; startLeaseKeepalive() renews at an interval and aborts after 30 stalled renewals with no progress; append(lease, entry) is token-fenced and annotations are lease-exempt.
verevonRelevance: A second, finer fence beneath the run lease; Verevon thread appends from multiple actors (users, agents, scheduled runs) need the same 'who may write now' rule.
notes: Quality 4: typed holders and progress-based keepalive (test/lease-keepalive.test.ts); complexity high for readers. Known sharp edge in the tape spec: the lease renews only on appends, so a silent step longer than five minutes can let another instance steal the session (docs/session-tape-spec.md:205-212).

name: Per-attempt tool-call result ledger for effectful control and surface calls (replay within one claim)
what: Effectful platform calls the agent makes (cron, webhook and similar control writes, posts, reactions) go through a ledger keyed by run, claim attempt and call order, so a call replayed within the same claim returns the recorded result instead of acting twice.
how: once() in tools/primitives.ts calls ToolLedger.begin(runId, attempt, callIndex) and returns the cached output when present, otherwise runs the call and record()s the JSON result; the tool_calls table has primary key (run_id, attempt, call_index) and the attempt is run.attempts, which increments on every claim, so a retried claim uses fresh keys. Duplicate effects across claims are handled elsewhere: the orchestrator replays an answer already recorded by a previous attempt (turn.already_answered) and resumes or re-runs the partial turn recorded on the tape. Migrations repair the primary key with checksummed maintenance steps.
verevonRelevance: Cheap model for Verevon's 'unknown effect' outcome: persist what a call returned per attempt and let verification, not blind retry, decide.
notes: Quality 3: narrower than first described: protects replays inside one claim only (test/tool-call-resume.test.ts, test/postgres-toolcalls-migration.test.ts). Corrected in the verification pass: an earlier draft claimed exactly-once effects across retries; the attempt is part of the key, so the ledger only protects replays inside one claim. SPEC lists webhook in-flight tracking across instances as an unfixed non-durability bug (qm#1943).

name: Steer and stop signals routed into the live run; orphaned signals replayed
what: A message sent while the agent is working becomes a steering input at the next step boundary, the word 'stop' aborts the run, and a steer that races with run completion is replayed as a new queued run instead of being lost.
how: routeWake() returns engage|steer|drop (halt, empty mid-turn, self); RunSignalStore stores abort|steer|client_result with dedupeKey, pending() and acknowledge(); app-turn checks whether the target run went terminal and calls replayOrphanedRunSignals() to find its own signal and queue a replay run; steer authors are recorded.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon room already supports mid-stream steer; the orphaned-signal replay closes the race that loses a steer when a run completes.
notes: Quality 4: orphaned-signal replay closes a real race (test/run-signal-store.test.ts, test/wake-steering.test.ts).

name: SSE run stream using AG-UI-style events with byte-offset text deltas
what: A browser or surface joins a running turn over Server-Sent Events and receives a start event, tool call start and result events, text deltas keyed by offset, a run snapshot, and a final run-finished event; the stream heals gaps by re-snapshotting.
how: GET /v1/runs/:id/events (auth source) writes RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, CUSTOM{name:delta,value:{offset,delta}}, CUSTOM{name:run} and RUN_FINISHED with SSE ids; sync/refresh bus events trigger snapshot catch-up; a 15 s heartbeat refresh, backpressure cap of 1 MiB (res.destroy) and x-accel-buffering:no; server events are fed to @tanstack/ai StreamProcessor on the client.
verevonRelevance: Resolves the scout's unverified AG-UI claim: the envelope is AG-UI-compatible even though the string 'AG-UI' is absent. Verevon's room polls every 6 s; an offset-delta SSE or NATS-to-SSE bridge with this event vocabulary would give push without a Convex client.
notes: Quality 4: small, tested stream contract with backpressure and offsets (test/run-events.test.ts, test/run-stream-events.test.ts); SSE only, no bidirectional channel. Correction to the t1 inventory: AG-UI event names (RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, RUN_FINISHED, TEXT_MESSAGE_*) are present in run-events.ts and core-bridge.ts. Uniqueness reviewed: the underlying technique is general engineering; it is distinctive mainly in how it is applied to agents in shared rooms.

name: Client-side stream recovery: offset checks, silence timeout, fallback polling, resync
what: If the stream goes quiet, opens late or skips ahead, the client abandons SSE and falls back to polling the run; on every reconnect of the shared event channel it refetches state, so a laptop sleep or proxy drop does not leave stale transcripts.
how: streamRunViaSse() aborts after SSE_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS or SSE_SILENCE_MS (30 s), returns 'fallback' when a delta offset exceeds the accumulated length, and applies terminal run snapshots with final results; subscribeDeliveries() calls onResync after any reopen and on server session_state_resync / inbox_resync events; session-state bus emits resync on LISTEN reconnect.
verevonRelevance: A concrete, testable resume protocol for the Space timeline; adopt 'offset deltas plus snapshot refresh plus resync-on-reopen'.
notes: Quality 4: offset check, silence timeout and polling fallback are all implemented client side (test/web-ui-sse.test.ts); no persistent offline state. No offline store, service worker or IndexedDB: drafts and layout use localStorage only (plugins/web-ui/src/drafts.ts).

name: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY event bus with one shared listener and resync on reconnect
what: Cross-process wakeups and UI state events ride Postgres NOTIFY: one dedicated LISTEN connection per process serves all subscribers, payloads are capped under the 8 KB limit (oversized events shed optional fields), and every reconnect triggers a resync callback.
how: createPostgresNotifyBus(channel) encodes JSON up to 7,500 bytes and drops larger events; subscribePostgresChannel() keeps a shared listener map keyed by connection string, LISTEN/UNLISTEN reconciled with retry every second and invokes resync after (re)subscribe; encodeWirePayload() sheds the participants list before dropping the event.
verevonRelevance: Verevon uses NATS for cross-plane events (best effort, no JetStream per the baseline); the lesson is the explicit resync callback and payload cap so lost notifications are repaired by re-reading state.
notes: Quality 4: handles size limits, reconnect and resync (test/postgres-listener.test.ts, test/postgres-listener-race.test.ts); notifications are only wake-ups by design. NOTIFY is lossy by design; the system depends on snapshot refresh and periodic polls (recoveryPollMs 5 s) for correctness.

name: One multiplexed SSE channel for presence of work across conversations
what: A single event stream tells the web app which conversations are working, awaiting approval, idle or changed, plus delivery nudges and inbox item changes, so the sidebar updates live without polling each session.
how: Core exposes GET /v1/session-state/events (event: session_state with threadRef, state working|awaiting_approval|idle|metadata, participants); the web-ui server relays it as /api/deliveries/events adding delivery and inbox_item events; participants are looked up server-side when shed; inbox item events are sent only to users who can see the loop.
verevonRelevance: This is the missing 'cross-room aggregate' for Verevon (baseline section 9: sidebar unread and presence aggregates absent); one filtered multiplexed stream beats per-room polling.
notes: Quality 4: one multiplexed stream with server-side participant lookup (test/session-state-events.test.ts); per-process fan-out limits not examined.

name: Durable delivery outbox with idempotency keys, claim TTL, overage expiry and shadow mode
what: Messages the agent or a schedule wants to deliver to a surface are written to a durable outbox with an idempotency key; a poller claims rows with a time-limited claim, acknowledges them, and drops undelivered rows after six hours instead of retrying forever.
how: DeliveryStore.enqueue() dedupes by idempotencyKey (and resurrects an expired undelivered row on re-enqueue), claimPending(type, ttl) hands out rows with claimedUntil, ack/ackByKey set deliveredAt and latency, DELIVERY_MAX_AGE_MS 6h expires stale rows, shadow rows are recorded but not delivered, recipient-thread and source-session provenance are stored; one contract test runs against memory and Postgres.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's target is at-least-once plus idempotent projection with explicit unknown; QM adds 'expire stale deliveries rather than retry forever' (a SPEC overengineering example) and shadow rows for dry-run comparison.
notes: Quality 4: contract tests run against memory and Postgres (test/delivery-store.test.ts, test/postgres-delivery-store.test.ts); SPEC calls the queue hand-rolled. SPEC:83 notes the custom claim and recovery logic is hand-rolled next to pg-boss.

name: Ack-after-durable gate for chat-platform events
what: For Slack the platform ack is held until the event is durably accepted (up to a 2.5 s cap); if the cap is hit the envelope is staged in a durable map within 300 ms, and if staging fails the ack is withheld so the platform redelivers; a sweeper replays stale staged envelopes with claim leases and a max-attempt budget.
how: createDeferredEnvelopeAck() with ACK_CAP_MS 2500 and AckGate.persisted()/failed(); createEnvelopeStaging() keyed slack:<account>:<type>:<channel>:<ts> using DurableMap.putIfAbsent, STAGE_TIMEOUT 300 ms, STALE 3 min, CLAIM 5 min, MAX_ATTEMPTS 5, ABANDON 24 h; replay gate reports persisted/failed.
verevonRelevance: The exact adapter-ingress discipline a Verevon Channel Plane (currently docs-only) would need: durable acceptance before acknowledgement, bounded staging fallback, replay sweeper.
notes: Quality 4: explicit timing constants and staged envelopes (test/slack-deferred-ack.test.ts, test/slack-envelope-staging.test.ts); Slack-specific. Twin-only E2E scenarios exercise event redelivery and dedupe. Uniqueness reviewed: the underlying technique is general engineering; it is distinctive mainly in how it is applied to agents in shared rooms.

name: Idempotency keys and replay windows at every ingress
what: Signed requests carry an event id and timestamp; duplicates within a five-minute window and stale timestamps are rejected; turns, cron fires, webhook receipts, swarm sends and deliveries all dedupe by a stable key.
how: createSourceAuth().verify() checks HMAC signature, 5-minute replay window (SOURCE_AUTH_REPLAY_WINDOW_MS) and ReplayDedupe.claim(eventId, expiry) with a Postgres variant; signing secrets must be at least 32 characters; IdempotencyStore and enqueue dedupKey are used by turns and triggers.
verevonRelevance: Standard but well executed; the shared signer in plugins/chassis is imported by every surface, which the Verevon plan wants as a generated protocol package.
notes: Quality 4: consistent across ingresses (test/source-auth.test.ts, test/postgres-replay-dedupe.test.ts); plain HMAC with a five-minute window. Plugins keep their own copies except plugins/chassis by repo rule (AGENTS.md).

name: Blue-green drain by build-heartbeat registry and a single background-owner record
what: During a deploy the older build stops claiming new runs once a newer build is heartbeating, finishes in-flight turns, and resumes claims if the newer build disappears; for AWS blue-green, one shared record names the single deployment allowed to run background work (Slack ingress, run claims, crons, maintenance).
how: instance_heartbeats table with buildSha/startedAt/beat_at; beat() returns true if a different build started later and beat within 30 s; DrainController.canClaim() = !superseded; background_ownership durable map with ownerDeploymentId; operator endpoint changes the owner and processes poll it; in-flight turns cut off at shutdown resume on the new tasks.
verevonRelevance: A low-tech way to do safe handover for Model Plane workers or a Space scheduler without a separate coordinator; the explicit owner record answers 'which stack owns schedules right now'.
notes: Quality 4: heartbeat drain and single owner record have drills (test/background-ownership.test.ts, test/postgres-instance-registry.test.ts); docs still describe a protocol older images used. ECS task protection was dropped in commit 6ca4d2c9 (2026-10-04); cli/README.md still describes it for older images (doc drift). Uniqueness reviewed: the underlying technique is general engineering; it is distinctive mainly in how it is applied to agents in shared rooms.

name: DurableMap: one generic JSON store with a memory twin for most small durable state
what: Feature flags, approvals, secret drops, mailboxes, swarms, principal links and many other small records share one storage abstraction backed by Postgres JSONB with atomic merge, update, mutateMany, putIfAbsent, take and select, and an in-memory implementation with the same contract for tests.
how: DurableMap<T> interface (get, put, putIfAbsent, insertIfAbsent, merge, update, mutateMany, deleteIf, take, select); jsonbStringify strips NUL and lone surrogates before writes because jsonb rejects them while memory maps accept them; tables are created lazily with idempotent DDL through the shared pool.
verevonRelevance: Pragmatic and cheap, but at Verevon scale each owner plane already has typed schemas; the transferable lesson is the contract-tested memory twin and the jsonb sanitization at the boundary.
notes: Quality 3: pragmatic and tested (test/durable-map-jsonb.test.ts, test/postgres-map.test.ts); a JSON-blob store trades schema discipline for speed. Over 60 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements across src; SPEC treats schema size and env count as KPIs to reduce.

name: Code-registered, checksummed migrations with pooled and session connection pools
what: Each module registers its own migrations with an id and expected checksum in code; a shared migration table records applied versions, migration runs on a dedicated one-connection pool, ordinary queries use a pooled endpoint (PgBouncer transaction mode) and only locks and LISTEN use direct session connections.
how: PG_MIGRATIONS_TABLE qm_schema_migrations; PgMigrationDefinition {id, statements, expectedChecksum, legacyId}; maintenance definitions can run before migrations; query timeouts use SET LOCAL inside a transaction; DATABASE_POOL_URL / DATABASE_DIRECT_POOL_MAX settings; scripts/test-pgbouncer.sh and a pgbouncer workflow exercise it.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Application and Model plane migrations on shared Postgres: splitting query and session pools is the part that bites when adopting PgBouncer.
notes: Quality 4: checksummed, retried migrations and pooler support (test/postgres-migrations.test.ts, test/pg-pool.test.ts); unusual but robust.

name: Large file transfer through presigned multipart blobs, off the model path
what: Uploads and downloads of attachments and published files move through presigned blob transfer with per-blob capability tokens and S3 multipart (16 MiB parts, 1 GB cap), so bytes never pass through the model or the chat transport.
how: BlobTransferStore with put/open and sha256 info; S3_PART_BYTES 16 MiB, MAX_BLOB_BYTES 1,000,000,000, MAX_STAGE_BLOB_BYTES 12 GB; routes /v1/blobs and /v1/files/uploads/:id/parts/:part and /complete; token audience blob-transfer carries direction and optional blob id; bucket lifecycle rules are checked.
verevonRelevance: Matches how Verevon should treat Space attachments (owner-plane object store plus short-lived transfer capability) rather than inline chat payloads.
notes: Quality 3: standard presigned multipart with caps (test/blob-transfer.test.ts).

name: Realtime non-features: no offline cache, no push gateway, no E2EE, no multi-device engine
what: QM has no service worker, IndexedDB cache, mobile push gateway, end-to-end encryption or multi-device sync engine; all content is server-side and clients refetch.
how: Negative greps over src, plugins, desktop and cli for serviceWorker, indexedDB, PushManager, Notification, libsodium/nacl/e2ee and push-gateway strings returned nothing; drafts and layout live in localStorage; the desktop app denies notification permission.
verevonRelevance: Teams, Slack and Grok Bot have these; Verevon should not look to QM for offline, push or E2EE, only for the resync and replay patterns above.
notes: Quality 1: negative result: no offline cache, push or E2EE, which peers do provide. NEG finding (grep-based, may miss renamed code); confidence medium. Qualified in the verification pass: small per-user UI preferences do sync through a server-side ui-state store (see that record); message and session content is simply refetched.

name: Session tape: append-only, model-view-first write-ahead log
what: Every conversation is one append-only log of exactly what the model read and produced, in consumption order, plus explicit context events (compaction, redaction, interrupt, model or harness change) and annotations; the model's context is a deterministic fold of the log for the current audience.
how: Tape rows are kind message (verbatim harness-native message with scope_label, bare_text, ts, hidden, overheard, author columns), context_event (compaction, redaction, interrupt, model_change, harness_change, legacy_import, legacy_patch) or annotation (approvals, watermarks); the harness appends at step boundaries synchronously under the writer lease (a failed append is turn-fatal); compaction carries a monotonicity guard; fold(rows, audience) is deterministic with no I/O; prompt envelopes are hash-deduplicated for forensics; images are stored by reference into the artifact store.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's chat threads and run checkpoints can adopt the invariant 'the model reads only what the log contains, in the order it read it' and the audience-parameterized fold; the explicit interrupt event is the interrupted-effect marker.
