notes: Quality 3 not 5: SPEC:172-176 and the Legacy-preservation lens record that session_entries and the tape both remain (SESSION_TAPE_MODE shadow|serve), 'stuck for weeks'; project sessions still use reconstruction and foreign-harness tapes stay shadow-only. Design is excellent, execution unfinished.

name: Org security posture (strict, auto, dangerous) with per-scope tightening and content-screen modes
what: An org picks how much the agent can do unattended: Strict pauses every tool call for approval, Auto (default) blocks private-network access, Dangerous removes approval gates; narrower scopes can only tighten. Content screening is a separate deployment mode (off, observe, enforce).
how: POSTURE_POLICIES maps posture to {toolApprovals none|all, denyPrivateNetworks}; resolveSecurityPolicy(posture, deploymentMode) caps screening at observe under Dangerous; composeSecurityPosture ranks dangerous<auto<strict; admin UI exposes posture, Auto flagger, approval grant options, command policy, ambient policy, sharing posture and egress policy per scope.
verevonRelevance: A small, legible vocabulary for agent autonomy per org and per Space that Verevon can map to its deny-by-default effect policies; strict vs auto vs dangerous also gives UI labels for room agent mode.
notes: Quality 4: three postures with per-scope tightening and an admin UI (test/security-posture.test.ts); posture defaults matter more than the mechanism. Added structure since the baseline: three knobs collapsed into SECURITY_SCREEN=off|observe|enforce (commit 4901e12f).

name: Prompt-injection screening: provenance-aware, chunked, external proxy contract
what: External content (inbound messages, attachments, skills, steering context, tool output from the outside world) is classified for prompt injection; the classifier can be a built-in model rubric or any HTTPS service that returns a score and threshold. Observe mode records only; enforce quarantines flagged content.
how: toolResultProvenance() labels results internal|workspace|external by tool (execute and web fetches are external); inputs are capped at 16,000 characters, split into overlapping 1,600-character chunks (256 overlap), at most two in flight, siblings cancelled on failure, responses capped at 64 KB with bounded retry backoff; any chunk at or above threshold makes the whole input Strict; each classification writes a security_screen.classify audit record without the text; outages and unscreenable content fail open with an untrusted-content marker in enforce mode.
verevonRelevance: The chunking, concurrency and audit-without-content shape is a ready spec for the Verevon cross-plane screening envelope; the fail-open default is the part to reject (Verevon must deny or degrade to read-only).
notes: Quality 3: provenance labelling and bounded concurrent chunks are tested (test/security-screener.test.ts); fails open on outages or unscreenable content. Doc change since the baseline: docs/deploy-directory.md now states that outages and timeouts fail open (commit 4901e12f, 2026-09-30), resolving the baseline's doc-vs-code contradiction by correcting the doc; the code is unchanged and still audits tool_result_failed_open.

name: Policy simulation: replay captured screenings through a candidate classifier configuration
what: An admin can test a new injection-classifier rubric or model against past real traffic before enabling it and see flagged, allowed, unscreened and error rates without seeing any payload.
how: POST /v1/admin/scopes/:scope/auto-flagger/test replays up to 500 recent captured screenings (sentinel step -1) with concurrency 4, 20 s per sample and a 120 s run deadline, returns counts and rates only; payloads stay with their conversations.
verevonRelevance: Dry-running a governance change against recorded traffic is a strong pattern for Verevon policy rows (space_effect_policies); add 'simulate this policy' before 'enable'.
notes: Quality 4: rare replay-based policy simulation with counts only (test/auto-flagger.test.ts). Uses retained captured LLM requests, which SECURITY.md:174-177 lists as a default-on retention risk.

name: Command policy floor (regex deny and require-approval rules)
what: Org rules force approval or denial for dangerous shell forms in every posture (recursive deletes, force push, DROP/TRUNCATE, fork bombs, curl-pipe-to-shell); scopes can add rules; matching normalizes quoting, ANSI-C escapes, heredocs and nested shell payloads to depth 8.
how: ORG_FLOOR_RULES + composePolicy(); scannableCommand() strips written heredocs, unquotes bare words, decodes $'..' escapes and recurses into executed payloads; evaluateCommand returns decision, reason, matched and an approvalKey that binds the binary plus the command at a boundary; tool descriptors can append rules but never allow.
verevonRelevance: The baseline already marks regex or shell-text command policy as 'do not copy as an authorization boundary'; use it only as a speed bump and keep typed owner-plane gates for effects.
notes: Quality 2: mistake catcher, not a boundary: SECURITY.md says obfuscation or write-then-execute can bypass it (test/command-policy.test.ts). SECURITY.md:133-136 itself says it is bypassable by obfuscation or write-then-execute. Quality 2 as a security boundary, 4 as a mistake-catcher.

name: Secret masking of execution output and structured diagnostics
what: Credential values injected for a command are masked out of the command's output and errors (including URL-encoded and base64 variants), and structured diagnostics redact sensitive keys, so secrets do not land in transcripts or logs.
how: createSecretValueMasker() builds needles for each secret env value (raw, encodeURIComponent, base64, base64url), ignores values under 8 characters and a short non-secret key list, replaces with <redacted:KEY>; createExactSecretValueMasker() for credential fields; MaskedExecutionError masks stack traces; redactStructuredDiagnostics redacts keys like token, password, authorization, cookie.
verevonRelevance: A cheap defense-in-depth layer for Space agent output when a secret is materialized; Verevon should prefer broker delivery so there is nothing to mask.
notes: Quality 3: covers raw, URL and base64 forms and structured diagnostics (test/secret-masking.test.ts); short or transformed secrets can still slip. Masking is value-based and cannot catch transformed or split secrets; SECURITY.md:146-149 says plaintext credentials remain readable inside the sandbox.

name: Audit log with idempotent writes, fire-and-forget default, and dedicated sinks
what: Security-relevant actions (screening, approvals, credential brokering, egress decisions, admin reads, cross-context reads, spend exports, impersonation) are recorded with principal, action, resource, scope and detail; separate sinks exist for credential usage, egress decisions and model-call metrics.
how: AuditLog.record() is non-blocking and logs-and-drops on a database failure (reportFailureAs); recordOnce(key, event) inserts with a partial unique index on idempotency_key; tail() filters by scope, action, since and resource substring; egress audit relays from the proxy in batches; credential usage and metrics sinks are separate stores; resource filter matches % and _ literally.
verevonRelevance: Confirms the baseline: do not copy the log-and-drop default; Verevon needs the outbox-backed audit obligation it already plans, plus QM's recordOnce idempotency key.
notes: Quality 3: idempotent writes and sinks exist (test/audit-log.test.ts, test/postgres-audit-log.test.ts) but the default is log-and-drop on database failure. Verified on main: record() swallows persist failures (postgres-audit-log.ts:65-77), exactly the pattern the Verevon plan lists under 'do not copy'.

name: Admin reads are audited but not consent-gated; retention controls are absent
what: A scope-authorized org admin can read transcripts, captured provider requests, documents, memory, connector metadata and mirrored message bodies; the read is audited. Sessions, memory and exact model-request captures persist by default and file artifacts have no expiry or reclamation.
how: SECURITY.md states admin reads are audited but require no user approval, request capture is on by default and artifact retirement and byte reclamation are not implemented; the admin 'retention' module computes DAU/WAU/MAU cohorts (product analytics), not data retention; the Retention and Metrics UI tabs were removed (commit b7994395).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Space deletion saga, ZDR propagation and retention classes are ahead of QM here; treat QM as the negative example (unbounded capture, no expiry).
notes: Quality 1: negative: admin reads without consent and no data retention or expiry controls (SECURITY.md). Correction to the t1 inventory: src/admin/retention.ts is a user-retention analytics report, so QM has no data-retention or legal-hold controls at all.

name: Principal links: one person, several sign-ins, with evidence and no privilege creation
what: A person's Slack id, email magic link and OIDC subject can be linked so credentials, grants, sessions, approvals and drops belong to one canonical principal; links are flat, evidence-recorded, reversible, never create admins, and deactivation follows the person.
how: principal_links durable map; personKey/samePerson fold linked ids to the canonical principal everywhere; admin API /v1/admin/principal-links with evidence; portal resolves GET /v1/principals/:id/canonical, caches one minute and returns 503 when core cannot answer; self-service Slack linking requires a signed ticket and ownership proof, email similarity is not proof.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Control owns identity, but the external-identity-link rules (flat, evidence, no admin escalation, fail closed on resolver outage) are a checklist for the planned Slack/Teams linking (plan S5.1).
notes: Quality 4: evidence-based linking without privilege creation (test/principal-links.test.ts).

name: Portal front door: sealed sessions with domain-separated keys, signed identity header, admin impersonation
what: A single public portal terminates sign-in (built-in email-code and password broker or external OIDC), issues HMAC-sealed session cookies, forwards only a signed identity header to private services, and lets admins impersonate a user with an explicit stop route.
how: seal()/open() use HMAC-SHA256 with keys derived by label (portal.session.v1, portal.desktop-login.v1); PortalIdentity header x-portal-identity carries p, authenticatedAs, imp and exp, verified with timingSafeEqual; session TTL defaults to 7 days (renew at half, 30-day cap); /v1/admin/impersonate and /stop; ImpersonationClaims record actor and target.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's gateway already owns session; the labelled-key derivation per cookie purpose and the explicit actor/target impersonation claims are cheap patterns to copy.
notes: Quality 3: domain-separated keys and constant-time checks (test/portal-plugin.test.ts, test/portal-identity.test.ts); a bespoke token format rather than a standard. Doc drift: SECURITY.md:190 says portal sessions default to eight hours, but code and plugins/portal/README.md:314 give 7 days (max 30 days).

name: Single-organization trust model, stated plainly
what: QM assumes one organization of authenticated internal users; guests and external users are outside the interaction boundary except through explicit exceptions, and QM is not a hardened multi-tenant or public service.
how: SECURITY.md Scope and Trust-boundary sections; ORG_ID env fixes the org; scope ids and tables are per org (org_id columns in policy tables) but isolation between orgs is not a design goal.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon baseline marks multi-tenancy as a Verevon lead; QM is a source of patterns for scope isolation inside one tenant, not for tenancy.
notes: Quality 2: honest statement of a narrow trust model; not a multi-tenant design. As a security reference QM is unusually honest: SECURITY.md enumerates its own limitations (command policy bypass, plaintext credentials, purposes not enforced, incomplete screening, audience-floor gaps, admin reads).

name: Capability-link published apps and isolated app origins
what: Published apps are private by default and shared separately (org, specific people, or 'anyone with the link'); external sharing needs an org admin to enable it; apps are served from isolated origins through the portal, and a capability link is swapped for a one-day cookie.
how: Deployment {ownerScopeId, createdInScope, defaultAudience, public} with share routes; external_app_sharing flag gates public links; viewer-session verifies portal cookies; app pages record views; apps can opt into framing by named origins (embed-ancestors); per-app acting-as credentials are limited by deployments flag on service credentials.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to future Verevon Studio/internal-app publishing (plan S5.4): owner versus creation-context scope on the artifact is the right data model; do not make bearer links the default sharing model.
notes: Quality 3: app links are bearer capabilities by design (SECURITY.md) with opt-in gating and isolated origins (test/deploy-access.test.ts, test/deploy-embed-ancestors.test.ts). SECURITY.md:179-183: links are bearer authorization and ACL changes do not revoke individual holders.

name: Org spend ledger, dashboard and token-authenticated export
what: An admin sees spend by day, scope, origin (live, cron, background) and model, with custom windows, and a finance system can pull the same ledger through a bearer-token export; each export is audited.
how: GET /v1/spend/export?from&to returns rows at the ledger grain with calls, costUsd and token counts (window at most 93 days, whole UTC days, half-open); route returns 404 unless SPEND_EXPORT_TOKEN is set; spend reports are served from saved daily totals; budgets (per principal and org rolling window) check input-token cost before a turn.
verevonRelevance: Verevon lacks cost per Space (baseline section 7); a ledger keyed by scope, origin and model is a ready model, and the export token pattern suits chargeback integrations.
notes: Quality 3: dashboard and token-gated export are tested (test/spend-export.test.ts, test/spend-summary.test.ts); export token is a single shared secret. SECURITY.md:184-189: the token is bearer authorization for org-wide spend. The enforced budget uses an input-token estimate only (estimateCostUsd), cruder than the dashboard ledger.

name: Supply-chain and process controls: cooldown, audit, provenance, independent review
what: New package versions must age seven days before entering a lockfile; production dependencies are audited in CI; images are signed and the CLI is published with npm provenance; CI rejects AI co-author trailers; every PR needs fresh-context reviewers per 'wall of shame' lens recorded in the PR description.
how: .npmrc min-release-age=7, npm audit --omit dev job, release workflows sign first-party images and pin digests into the published package, a coauthor-trailers job, and a wall-of-shame workflow that fails until the PR body lists a verdict and score per lens for the head commit.
verevonRelevance: The lens catalogue (overengineering, band-aid, duplication, non-durability, config-matrix, god files, regex) plus mandatory independent reviewers is a ready-made engineering policy for AI-authored Verevon code.
notes: Quality 4: dependency cooldown, signing, provenance and a CI-enforced review report are real controls (test/wall-of-shame-check.test.ts); process-heavy. Note the repo violates its own zero-comments rule in places (for example src/harness/goal.ts header, src/resolution/turn-context.ts). The repo also tracks screenshots despite its own ban (desktop/test/screenshots/*.png, docs/qa/execution-credentials/*.png, docs/qa/tool-purpose/*.png), which shows how hard these rules are to hold.

name: Typed secret routing and deployment conformance
what: Each first-party service publishes a typed secret schema; the CLI computes which secrets each task receives and renders .env.example with names only; operators push values to Fly secrets or AWS Secrets Manager; doctor and conformance commands verify prerequisites and that the live deployment layer matches the directory by content hash.
how: SecretSpec schemas per service and feature predicate; qm secrets push uploads without printing; core validates required secrets at production boot (distinct DEPLOYMENT_CONTROL_SECRET, 32+ characters); conformance compares the live deployment-layer contentHash and descriptors with the directory bundle; unknown contract majors fail closed.
verevonRelevance: Fits the Verevon plan for one release contract spanning plane image digests, schema versions and secret targets; conformance by content hash is the cheap runtime half.
notes: Quality 4: typed secret schemas and drift tests (test/secret-schema-conformance.test.ts, test/secret-schema-drift.test.ts). Documents a v1 contract with a 'clause status' table (docs/deploy-directory.md:138) so unimplemented clauses are explicit.

name: AWS release safety: restore-point proof, rollout deadline with auto-rollback, digest pins
what: Before mutating an AWS stack the CLI proves the database has a current point-in-time restore point and records it in the manifest; it waits for each rolling service to complete within a deadline and rolls back changed services on timeout; releases pin immutable image digests and rollback restores code and configuration while printing the matching data restore point.
how: up verifies RDS LatestRestorableTime lag (QM_AWS_DB_MAX_RESTORE_LAG_MS 10 min) and retention before the first mutation; polls to COMPLETED within QM_AWS_ROLLOUT_DEADLINE_MS (20 min); rollback prints the restore point; live checks use an authenticated canary that needs a real model reply, session persistence, generated title and database catalog health, bound to the responding process; terraform module behind CloudFront with portal as sole ALB target.
verevonRelevance: A concrete release-gate checklist (restore-point proof, canary with real model reply, owner handover) for the Verevon R-5 immutable release and rollback rehearsal.
notes: Quality 4: restore-point proof and deadline-based rollback are implemented with drills (test/aws-recovery-drills.test.ts); AWS code is a 4,800-line file. Single-org per stack; multi-tenant SaaS operation is not addressed. The rollout deadline default is 20 minutes when polling service targets but 30 minutes for the background-ownership handoff (cli/src/backends/aws.ts:1487, 3329, 3341).

name: Self-hosted per-org deployment as the multi-tenancy answer
what: Instead of multi-tenant isolation, each organization deploys its own stack in its own cloud account, driven from a committed deployment directory (config, sandbox tools and skills, plugin images, infra) pinned to an exact CLI/runtime version; a hosted third-party (Agent37) option exists.
how: qm init materializes qm.config.jsonc, .env.example, sandbox/, plugins/, infra/ (Terraform on AWS) and an agent-runnable runbook; deploy/layers/<org> keeps org-private material in a source fork; targets docker, fly, aws, with Helm and Porter for clusters; package deployments pin @yc-software/qm and published image digests, source forks use update-qm and upstream-pr.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is a multi-tenant platform, so this is mainly a packaging reference for dedicated-tenant or on-prem editions; the agent-readable runbook (deployment.md and .codex/skills/deploy-qm) is a smart delivery format.
notes: Quality 4: deliberate answer to multi-tenancy with a tested chart and CLI (test/helm-chart.test.ts); shifts operations to every customer. Operators carry the burden: 285 env knobs referenced in src/config.ts and per-provider matrices.

name: Test strategy: sharded tests, real-Postgres lane, exact-tree CI reuse, boot smoke, certified tree
what: CI shards the 712 root tests five ways, runs a separate real-Postgres durability and cross-process lane, boots each plugin's production image, skips re-running checks on main when the merged tree equals the tested PR tree, and records an immutable tested-tree receipt.
how: node --test with --experimental-test-module-mocks; test:root:shard with a shard-plan check; test:pg lists about 50 Postgres test files; scripts/smoke-surface-image.sh boots admin, web-ui, auth and portal images; the reuse job proves the exact tree passed before; certify records the tested tree; fakes exist for every sandbox provider; route-table-driven auth parity tests.
verevonRelevance: Cheap wins to copy: contract tests run against memory and Postgres implementations, route-auth drift tests, fake providers, and the exact-tree reuse job.
notes: Quality 4: sharded, real-Postgres and boot-smoke lanes plus exact-tree reuse; SPEC leaves the over-testing lens undescribed. Taxonomy has no testing category; mapped here as assurance. SPEC lists 'Over-testing' with description pending.

name: Slack digital-twin E2E with event pump and LLM-judged assertions
what: Post-merge scenarios drive a real Slack workspace as real users, or run fully parallel against an isolated Slack digital twin; a poller delivers recorded events, signed and per-channel ordered, to the instance, and scenarios assert on unforgeable run markers and LLM-judged replies; twin-only scenarios cover event redelivery, mid-session revocation and rate limits.
how: test/live-slack/run.ts lanes (parallel, serial DM, exclusive), retries once (flaky still green), shardable by LIVE_E2E_SHARD, scenarios tagged @smoke/@twin; arga.ts provisions the twin and seeds alice/bob/carol; startEventPump stamps channel_type and synthesizes app_mention events to paper over fidelity gaps.
verevonRelevance: A channel adapter needs exactly this: a twin of the platform plus event replay; for a future Verevon Slack or Teams adapter (Channel Plane) it makes ack/redelivery behavior testable in CI.
notes: Quality 4: digital-twin Slack with LLM-judged assertions is unusual and documented (test/arga-provisioning.test.ts); fidelity gaps are patched by an event pump. Depends on an external twin vendor (Arga) and live Slack credentials.

name: Slack is the human chat system of record; QM sessions are the agent's conversation log
what: QM does not implement human-to-human messaging: people talk to each other in Slack, and QM stores agent conversations as sessions that Slack and the web UI both project. On the web, a project is a shared agent session with a member roster, optionally linked to a Slack channel; sharing a conversation outside is a read-only snapshot.
how: SPEC: the tokens sent to the model are the single source of truth and Slack and web are projections of the same sessions; Conversation kinds are dm, channel, group; web Project {memberIds, channelMemberIds, slackChannel} maps to group:web-project-<id>; session sharing creates a read-only snapshot, not a live room; Slack history is mirrored into channel_messages for ambient judgment and search.
verevonRelevance: The key contrast for the Space: Verevon must own multi-human conversation itself (humans, agents and threads in one room) because QM offloads it to Slack; QM supplies the projection principle and the agent-side plumbing, not a chat engine.
notes: Quality 2 as a messaging core (no reactions, edits, typing, presence, read state or polls of its own); high as an agent-harness surface.

name: Surface-neutral message cache with ingest events and live fallback
what: Messages from the chat platform are mirrored into a neutral store (container, ts, thread, author, text, files, mentions, edited/deleted, handled) that the agent can read, search and judge ambient batches against, with a live fallback to the platform for gaps.
how: channel_messages, channel_state and channel_files tables behind a SurfaceCache interface (pushSurfaceEvents, readMessages, search, active threads); IngestEvent normalizes Slack payloads (including forwarded content, tombstones, thread broadcasts); history backfill is rate limited; mirror fidelity is covered by a Postgres test.
verevonRelevance: Gives a Verevon Channel Plane the shape of a normalized external-message projection; inside Verevon the equivalent would be an Application-plane conversation store with the same fields plus Control audience.
notes: Quality 3: tested mirror with live fallback (test/surface-cache.test.ts, test/slack-mirror-fidelity.test.ts); admins can read mirrored bodies. Admins can read mirrored message bodies (SECURITY.md:170-173).

name: Human edits and deletes surface to the agent as revision entries
what: When a person edits or deletes a message the agent already saw, a revision note is appended to the conversation so the model's view stays aligned with what is on screen.
how: messageRevision()/renderMessageRevision() produce a system entry kind message_revision {action edited|deleted, ts, text} rendered as XML-like attributes; revisions are appended outside a turn using appendEntryOutsideTurn with the session lease; Slack cut/pin/delete deliveries are repeated with state checks.
verevonRelevance: When Space adds message edit/delete, the agent needs the same signal so it does not reason over text a human retracted; the append-outside-turn under lease pattern avoids racing a running turn.
notes: Quality 3: small and correct (test/message-revisions.test.ts).

name: Fork a conversation from a chosen message
what: A user can branch a conversation at a message to continue it separately; the fork copies only what the forking viewer can see.
how: Session.forkedFrom and forkBoundarySeq; /v1/sessions/:id/fork; forkSession copies a viewer's folded projection into a fresh tape as a legacy_import event, the one sanctioned projection-to-tape path; fork holds the 'fork' session lease holder.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon plan lists visibility-preserving fork as S1.7; QM's rule (copy the viewer's audience-folded view, not the raw log) is the safe default.
notes: Quality 3: uses the sanctioned projection-to-tape path (test/session-fork.test.ts).

name: Directory visibility rules and tri-state membership with safe fallback
what: Who can see or be reached in a DM, group or channel is decided from a directory: DMs are owner-only, groups need membership, public channels are visible, private channels need membership; when the directory cannot answer, membership falls back to a conservative rule instead of guessing.
how: isVisible(dir, actor, target) switch on dm|group|channel; sharedScopeMembership() returns true|false|undefined (unknown) and memberOfSharedScope() falls back to session participation only when unknown; currentSharedScopeMember resolves several id spellings; withLiveTurnMembership lets the verified live speaker count as a member of the turn's scope.
verevonRelevance: Verevon baseline already notes 'do not use historical session participation as an authorization fallback'; the useful part is the explicit unknown state, which should map to deny or read-only.
notes: Quality 3: tri-state membership with safe fallback (test/visibility.test.ts, test/scope-membership-live-roster.test.ts). The session-participation fallback is exactly the pattern the Verevon plan lists under 'do not copy'.

name: Versioned project roster with Slack channel link and fenced turn admission
what: A web project has an owner and members, can be linked to a Slack channel whose membership syncs in, and every turn or enqueue is admitted under the current roster version so stale work cannot land after a membership change.
how: Project {ownerId, memberIds, channelMemberIds, slackChannel}; ManagedGroupDirectory exposes version(groupId) and withVersion(groupId, version, fn); withRosterLock serializes roster mutations; app-turn wraps enqueue and steering in withCurrentProjectRoster and refuses with 'project membership changed; retry from the current project'.
verevonRelevance: The baseline's P0 'versioned authority fencing' pattern: compare membership/authority revision immediately before an effect and refuse stale work; Verevon should carry Control's aggregate revision the same way.
notes: Quality 4: versioned roster fences admission (test/projects.test.ts); project-only. Project group refs are string-encoded (group:web-project-*), which the Verevon plan lists as do-not-copy; use typed ids.

name: Team scopes: org-defined groups that contribute shared resources to a turn
what: An admin can define teams with members and admins and attach rooms to them; a team's read-only files and credentials join a turn when the person is on the team and the room is configured for it, everyone present is on it, or Open posture applies and the team is not isolated in Open.
how: teams, team_members (role member|admin) and team_rooms tables; teamsForTurn() applies ownScope || configured || everyoneOn || (open && !isolatedInOpen); the resolver mounts team layers read-only at team-<id>; the prompt gets a note naming ambiguity rules when two teams provide the same resource name; feature flag team_scopes.
verevonRelevance: Verevon org-core has no teams (baseline section 2). QM teams are resource-sharing groups, not chat groups: a model for 'team-owned skills, credentials and files' that Spaces can reference.
notes: Quality 3: flagged and recent (test/teams.test.ts, test/postgres-teams.test.ts). Added 2026-10-11, one day before HEAD; flagged and young. Applied through an Admin API passed the team store only in commit 0b37830c.

name: Participant tenure windows on shared conversations
what: Each participant of a shared conversation sees only entries from when they joined (and until they left), measured by sequence number or time.
how: ParticipantWindow {sessionId, principalId, validFrom, validTo, validFromSeq, validToSeq}; entryWithinTenure() prefers sequence bounds; participantWindowsOf/listParticipants back transcript reads and spend attribution; approvals outside a member's tenure are refused.
verevonRelevance: Answers the Space question 'what does a late joiner see?' with a concrete rule; pair it with a context cutoff checkpoint when audience changes.
notes: Quality 4: sequence-bounded windows (documented in the tape spec); limited tests found. Project sessions use member-inherits-history in some paths (docs/memory-records.md:90) so the rule is not uniform.

name: Scope-to-scope resource grants over files, skills, apps, crons and service credentials
what: A scope can grant another scope read or write access to a specific resource (file path, skill, deployed app, cron, service credential); in a shared room a granted resource is available only if every participant is entitled.
how: Grant {ownerScopeId, granteeScopeId, ref, permission read|write}; ResourceRef kinds file, skill, deploy, cron, service-cred with prefixed encodings; AclStore.handlesForAudience() and sharedOfKindForAudience() apply the audience filter; Postgres grant store; /v1/grants and /v1/grants/revoke.
verevonRelevance: Matches the Verevon rule that Space membership never widens an owner-plane ACL: shared resources need explicit owner grants, evaluated against the whole audience.
notes: Quality 3: straightforward grants with Postgres store (test/acl-revoke-authz.test.ts, test/postgres-grant-store.test.ts). Permission is only read|write; there is no manage/share level (Google-Docs style is a stated artifact goal in docs/SPEC.md:31).

name: Admin console, invites and onboarding as first-class modules
what: An org admin has a console for users (invite, deactivate, reset, impersonate), spend, governance, integrations, keychain, skills and artifacts, transcripts, activity and branding; invited teammates receive single-use sign-in links and a per-user onboarding checklist with a skill-driven welcome.
how: plugins/admin/ui modules (users, user-detail, spend, governance, integrations, keychain, artifacts, transcript, activity, history, settings); /v1/admin/users/invite and /v1/auth/invitations/redeem; /v1/admin/users/:principalId/onboarding; Slack bot onboarding checklist; branding via ORG_BRAND_* and an admin Branding card.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has org members, invites and RBAC; the transferable idea is an onboarding skill that runs inside the product and per-user onboarding state exposed to admins.
notes: Quality 3: functional admin console and invite flow (test/admin-users.test.ts); UI duplicates web UI patterns per SPEC. docs/SPEC.md:128-135 flags admin UI versus web UI mismatch as a recurring defect.

name: Notifications are delivery to a destination; no push, mute or do-not-disturb
what: Anything the agent or a schedule wants someone to see is a delivery to a destination (a Slack DM, thread or channel, or a web session); there are no browser or mobile push notifications, no mute or snooze, and no unread counts per conversation.
how: principalDestination(target, onBehalfOf) builds a person DM destination; DeliveryStore queues and acknowledges; the desktop app denies the Notification permission; negative greps for Notification, PushManager, serviceWorker, snooze and mute found none; count badges exist only on Crons and Apps.
verevonRelevance: Teams, Slack and Grok Bot all have attention management; Verevon should look to those and to Novu-backed notification-core, not QM.
notes: Quality 1: negative: delivery to a destination only; no push, mute or do-not-disturb. NEG finding; QM leans on Slack for attention routing.

name: Pluggable search backends with per-backend failure reporting; indexed conversation search
what: Global search fans out to registered backends and returns hits plus the names of backends that failed; the web command palette searches skills, crons, apps, projects and webhooks and shows failed or limited sources; conversation history has an indexed entry search the agent can also use.
how: createCoreSearch(backends) with SearchBackend {name, search}; hit types message|conversation|file|page|external; /v1/search, /v1/resources/search, /v1/sessions/search; ResourceSearchResponse has failed[] and limited[]; indexed conversation search exposed through the sessions tool (commit ada7af76); materialization barriers removed (1ea3e28b).
verevonRelevance: Verevon search must stay owner-plane and ZDR-aware; the explicit failedBackends and limited arrays are a good 'gap, not empty' contract for cross-plane search.
notes: Quality 3: pluggable with explicit partial failure (test/core-search.test.ts, test/search-index.test.ts); no semantic answer UI. No semantic or AI-answer search over documents; memory recall is the nearest equivalent.

name: Deployment layer: sandbox tool descriptors and skills delivered by content hash
what: An operator ships tools and skills for the agent computer as a directory (tool.json descriptors, binaries or install files, SKILL.md trees); the layer is versioned by content hash, synced to core, converged onto every sandbox backend on each provision, and checked by conformance.
how: tool.json fields: label, advertise, hints, auth.check/reauth/credentialPaths, egress, approvals (deny or require approval only), install.binary and install.files (text files under /usr/local/bin or lib with mode); PUT /v1/deployment-layer stores the bundle in Postgres with canonical SHA-256; removed layer-owned skills are archived; Sprites boxes boot a stock image and receive the layer through sync.
verevonRelevance: A clean extension contract for 'org-specific tools and skills for the agent PC' without forking core; descriptors that can only tighten policy are the safe-extension pattern for Space agent bindings.
notes: Quality 4: content-hashed layers with conformance (test/deployment-layer-store.test.ts, test/deployment-layer-routes.test.ts).

name: Admin-registered MCP servers with shared or per-user credentials
what: An admin registers HTTP MCP servers whose tools become agent tools; each server uses either one shared credential or the initiating person's own token from the encrypted keychain, and can be marked read-only.
how: PUT /v1/admin/mcp-servers/:id with credentialScope shared|per-user, credentialHost and credentialAccountType (default, personal, company), readOnly and enabled; the runtime supplies the actor and tool arguments cannot select another user; the client speaks JSON-RPC over HTTP (JSON or SSE responses) with none, bearer or OAuth client-credentials auth and refuses redirects.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has user/private/shared/org MCP ownership (baseline); QM's rule that the runtime supplies the actor and arguments cannot name another user belongs in the Space tool-call path.
notes: Quality 3: shared and per-user credentials with refusal of redirects (test/mcp-admin.test.ts, test/mcp-connectors.test.ts). QM exposes no MCP server of its own (no registerTool or StreamableHTTP server in src).

name: Connected-app OAuth with callback identity verification (Composio)
what: People connect third-party apps through consent links; execution is bound to the canonical principal, verifies account owner, active status and tool version before every call, never retries an uncertain execution, and callback verification ensures a forwarded consent link cannot attach the wrong human's account.
how: Backend derives the Composio user id from org and canonical principal; /v1/composio identity, toolkits, tools, authorize, execute, connections; the web surface passes session_uri to core which completes auth with the signed-in user's derived identity; original return URL and expiry are stored durably per principal and account; agent calls require the current running turn lease; audit records exclude arguments and bodies.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to integration-corev2 OAuth: bind consent to the initiating principal and verify at callback, and never auto-retry an uncertain external execution.
notes: Quality 4: identity-verified callback and lease check (test/composio-route.test.ts); third-party dependent. Composio keys stay in the backend (commit 97e44a22); 'never retry uncertain execution' mirrors the unknown-effect rule.

name: Inbound webhooks with provider verifiers, wake envelopes and run-as-owner execution
what: A webhook endpoint belongs to a scope owner, verifies the sender's signature (HMAC-SHA256 plus provider-specific verifiers and handshakes), derives a delivery id for deduplication, wraps the payload as untrusted data and runs the owner's task like a cron fire.
how: WebhookReceiver.deliver(id, {headers, rawBody}) returns 202|200 (handshake)|401|404; Verifier {verify, deliveryId, handshake}; form-encoded and JSON bodies parsed; payload capped at 16,000 characters inside a wake envelope; processing uses runTrigger with the owner's authority; routes /v1/webhooks/incoming/:id plus enable, disable and events.
verevonRelevance: A reference for integration events entering a Space as agent triggers; reuse the wake-envelope idea (payload labelled untrusted) with Verevon's provenance envelope.
notes: Quality 3: provider verifiers and 202 semantics (test/webhook-receiver.test.ts, test/webhook-verifiers.test.ts); SPEC records a cross-instance in-flight race still open. docs/SPEC.md:95 notes in-flight dedupe for webhooks was process-local (qm#1943 proposes shared Postgres claims); outbound webhooks are absent.

name: Plugins as separate signed-HTTP services over a shared chassis
what: The web UI, admin, portal, auth broker and Slack surface are separate packages that call core over signed HTTP and never import core code; one shared chassis package holds the sanctioned plumbing (signer, core client, router, claims, failure copy), and the CLI discovers organization plugins from a plugins/ folder of Dockerfiles or prebuilt images.
how: AGENTS.md forbids plugins importing core except plugins/chassis; chassis exports source-auth-sign, core-client, router, portal-identity, branding, claims; discoverPlugins() merges source folders and image entries, rejects both, validates names, supports coreAccess and typed secrets; admin and auth are embedded modules of web-ui and portal (combined services).
verevonRelevance: Supports the Verevon plan to generate a shared surface protocol package instead of duplicating signer code; also a template for external surface adapters (Slack, Teams) as services over the same contract.
notes: Quality 4: enforced import boundary with a shared chassis; SPEC notes the web server entrypoint is a god file.

name: Skills as slash commands in the web composer
what: Typing / in the web composer opens a picker of the person's visible skills and inserts the skill name into the draft; the agent resolves it through the skill tool. The Slack surface has no slash commands.
how: SLASH_TOKEN regex over the draft, matchSkills() sorts by match position, loadSkills() fetches /api/skills once and caches; acceptSkill() writes '/name ' into the draft; no server-side command parsing and no app.command handler in the Slack plugin.
verevonRelevance: Correction to the t1 NEG that slash commands are absent: they exist in the web composer as a skill picker. A cheap Space composer feature (type / to pick an agent skill or agent) without any new command protocol.
notes: Quality 3: client-only completion; no server-side command registry. Text token only; behaviour depends on the model honoring the inserted skill name.

name: Custom model providers and an authenticated model gateway with discovery
what: An org can add custom model providers (Responses protocol) or route all model calls through a gateway such as LiteLLM; models are discovered from the gateway's authenticated metadata endpoints, namespaced, and refreshed every five minutes with fail-safe behavior.
how: MODEL_GATEWAY_URL/API_KEY/API_KEY_HEADER; discovery via GET /v1/models and /model_group/info keeping only chat models with tool support and valid pricing metadata; groups of only Anthropic providers use native Messages to preserve signed thinking blocks; a failed refresh disables gateway routes without affecting direct providers; /v1/admin/custom-providers.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Model Plane already owns routing and cost; the discovery-with-pricing-metadata gate is a good admission rule for any model offered to Space agents.
notes: Quality 3: protocol selection from provider metadata, not names (test/gateway-discovery-e2e.test.ts, test/model-gateway.test.ts).

name: Published web apps: versioned deployments owned by a scope, hosted by pluggable providers
what: Agents can build and publish internal web apps that are versioned, rolled back, renamed, archived, shared (org, people, link) and hosted by Docker, AWS, Fly or Porter; apps have an owner scope separate from the scope they were created in.
how: Deployment {ownerScopeId, createdInScope, currentVersion, versions[], status, endpoint, alwaysOn, embedAncestors, public}; DeployProvider {apply, reconcile, destroy, setAlwaysOn, resolveEndpoint, logs} with a managedScaleToZero profile; /v1/deployments routes for fetch, logs, git-url, share, rollback, redeploy, archive, restore, name, display-name, always-on, embed-ancestors; a git HTTP broker lets apps be edited by repository.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Studio is gateway-local and in-memory (baseline section 8); QM's owner-versus-creation scope split and provider interface are the model for a governed internal-app lifecycle (plan S5.4).
notes: Quality 4: many tests (test/deploy-store.test.ts, test/deploy-redeploy-route.test.ts) and several providers; still accumulating drift between providers. Four deploy providers add to the config matrix (docs/SPEC.md:97-111).

name: SHA-addressed file artifacts with owner scope and creation context
what: Files the agent publishes or receives are registered as artifacts with owner scope, creator, path, mimetype, size and SHA-256, kept in durable object storage and shareable by grant; direct upload protocol and recovery are documented.
how: FileArtifact {id, ownerScopeId, createdBy, path, mimetype, sizeBytes, blobKey, sha256, direction, source, createdInScope}; DurableByteStore for bytes; /v1/files, /v1/files/:id/content, direct multipart uploads; recurring job checkpoints are stored as Files instead of sandbox disk.
verevonRelevance: Matches the baseline provenance-bearing artifact pattern; Verevon should keep Data Plane as the owner and carry owner/created-in/actor metadata, with expiry and reclamation QM lacks.
notes: Quality 3: simple and sound (test/file-artifact-store.test.ts); no expiry or reclamation. SECURITY.md:174-178: no expiry, no artifact retirement or byte reclamation.

name: Read-only session share snapshots with allowlisted content
what: A conversation can be shared as an immutable snapshot (anyone in the org or anyone with the link) built from an allowlist of user messages, final replies and attachments, never thinking, tool output or raw payloads; attachments are copied into separate share storage and the link dies if the creator loses access.
how: session_shares durable map keyed by an unguessable token; share-specific file ids authorize only copied files; internal and external reads re-verify the creator is still internal and can access the original entries; isolated frontend entry with no session fetches, no-store, no-referrer, noindex and a strict CSP.
verevonRelevance: A safe way to export a Space thread to outsiders (customers, auditors) without exposing tool traces; the allowlist projection plus creator-access revalidation is worth copying.
notes: Quality 4: re-verifies the creator on every read (test/session-sharing.test.ts, test/web-ui-shared-threads.test.ts). Existing links cannot be revoked (docs/session-sharing.md:3).

name: Playground artifacts: validated HTML previews authored by the agent
what: The agent can produce a self-contained HTML playground that is validated before it is registered and shown in chat or the apps list.
how: createPlaygroundArtifact() with validatePlaygroundHtml(); the miniapp skill instructs the format; shared pages render in an isolated frame.
verevonRelevance: A lightweight interactive artifact type for a Space canvas without a hosting pipeline.
notes: Quality 2: narrow validated preview path (test/playground.test.ts). Only the module header and skill were read; behavior of validation rules not traced.

name: One conversation log, projected per surface
what: The same session renders as Slack messages, task cards and reactions in Slack, and as a transcript with thinking, tool rows, subagent chips and approvals on the web; agents see Slack mrkdwn and web markdown conversions at the edges.
how: presenters in src/slack (mrkdwn conversion, ack and task presenters, approval cards) read core session and run state; web uses activity-presentation, subagent-activity, working-dot and work-duration modules over the same runs; conversationView serializes Slack threads for the model.
verevonRelevance: A Space chat, a future Slack mirror and the run console should be projections of one thread/run model rather than separate stores.
notes: Quality 3: separate presenters over one log (test/slack-presenters.test.ts); duplicate logic per surface persists. docs/SPEC.md:128-135 lists mismatched UI between surfaces as a recurring defect.

name: Scope-centred context page and split-pane multiview
what: The web UI has a page per scope (personal, project, channel, group) with conversations, people, Slack link and grouped resources; sessions can be tiled into up to 16 draggable panes (dockview) with restorable layouts.
how: contexts.ts renders contextMeta(scope) panels (Conversations, Slack channel, People, resource groups); split-layout.ts MAX_TILES = MAX_PANES = 16 with v1 pane seeds; split.ts builds the dockview-core grid; deep links address a context by scope and a chat by session.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon baseline recommends building Space tabs from the scope-centered resource UI; the multi-pane watch-several-agents layout suits a Chief/Core console.
notes: Quality 3: scope-centred page is coherent, but SPEC's god-file lens names chat.ts and the Browse pages are inconsistent (test/web-contexts.test.ts). Mismatched-UI lens: Browse tabs for skills, crons, apps, files each developed their own filters (docs/SPEC.md:132-133).

name: Thin Electron shell around the remote web deployment with a locked-down renderer
what: The desktop app loads the same web UI from the org's QM instance in a sandboxed window with its own persistent cookie partition per instance, no Node access, all device permissions denied, webviews blocked, off-origin links opened in the browser and same-instance links opened in sandboxed preview windows that share the session.
how: BrowserWindow with nodeIntegration false, contextIsolation true, sandbox true; session = fromPartition(persist:qm-<origin>); setPermissionRequestHandler and setPermissionCheckHandler return false; will-attach-webview prevented; will-navigate/will-redirect intercept auth routes (hand off to browser sign-in) and external URLs; setWindowOpenHandler allows only same-origin child windows with the same sandbox settings; instance URL must be HTTPS (HTTP only for localhost) and carry no credentials.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 is a web SPA with no native shell (UI baseline section 11); this is a compact, security-first template for a Tauri or Electron shell that wraps the existing gateway-fronted app without bundling a backend.
notes: Quality 4: locked-down renderer, sender validation and a real Electron navigation test; prototype scope. Prototype status: no auto-update, no tray, no native notifications, mic and camera denied, unsigned macOS build unless a release identity is supplied. Per the t1 Slack and Grok Bot inventories those peers ship richer native shells (not re-verified in this audit).

name: PKCE-style browser sign-in handoff with a single-use deep-link code
what: Sign-in happens in the user's real browser (so password managers, passkeys and SSO cookies work); the app receives a two-minute single-use code through a qm-desktop:// link and redeems it with a proof key, so credentials never enter the app.
how: createLogin() makes a random verifier and state and sends the S256 challenge to /auth/desktop; the portal mints a sealed desktop-login token bound to challenge, state, audience origin, session expiry and a jti with at most 120 s lifetime; loginCallback() validates protocol, host, path, state and code size; the app POSTs code, verifier and state to /auth/desktop/redeem with an Origin header; redemption uses the durable core claim store to prevent replay across portal instances; attempts expire after 10 minutes and are cancelled when the window closes.
verevonRelevance: A drop-in design for Verevon desktop or mobile sign-in against Control/auth-core: deep-link return, PKCE binding and single-use claim in the shared store.
notes: Quality 4: PKCE-like handoff with single-use code and replay protection, tested in desktop and portal tests. The same flow handles trusted OIDC entry and preserves the original authentication time and expiry.

name: Single-instance lock, custom protocol and instance chooser
what: The app registers the qm-desktop protocol, forces a single running instance, forwards deep links from a second launch to the first, and lets the user connect or switch to a different QM instance from a welcome screen.
how: requestSingleInstanceLock, setAsDefaultProtocolClient('qm-desktop'), app.on('open-url') and 'second-instance' route callbacks to finishBrowserSignIn; instance URL persisted to userData/instance.json with mode 0600; QM_DESKTOP_URL env override; Change Instance menu item (CmdOrCtrl+,); packager registers the scheme.
verevonRelevance: Standard desktop plumbing; Verevon multi-org users will need the same per-instance partition and workspace switch.
notes: Quality 3: standard Electron conventions. Multi-account is per instance (one signed-in account per instance partition); no in-app multi-account switcher.

name: Sender-validated IPC with a minimal exposed surface
what: The renderer can only call three narrow operations from the setup screen and one 'open in browser' operation from workspace windows; each handler checks the sender window, frame and origin before acting.
how: ipcMain.handle('qm:open-browser') requires the sender to be one of the tracked workspace windows, the main frame, an origin equal to the instance origin and an http(s) same-origin destination; setup handlers use assertSetup(event) comparing sender and senderFrame URL to the packaged setup page; preload exposes window.qm (login status, current instance, connect) and window.qmDesktop.openBrowser only.
verevonRelevance: A good least-privilege IPC baseline for any Verevon desktop shell; the Grok Bot t1 inventory records only two sender-validation observations among 15 IPC operations, so QM is the cleaner reference here.
notes: Quality 4: minimal surface with sender validation; tests present in desktop/test.

name: Desktop ergonomics injected by preload: drag regions, tab cycling and hold-Command session shortcuts
what: On macOS the sidebar header becomes the title bar; holding Command (Control elsewhere) reveals numbered shortcuts for the first nine visible sessions and 1 to 9 switches; Control+Tab, Control+PageUp/Down and platform chords cycle panes; Alt+Left/Right navigate history.
how: workspace-preload injects a style block keyed on data-qm-desktop, annotates session links with data-qm-shortcut, handles keydown/keyup in capture phase while no dialog is open, and a MutationObserver refreshes the list; main forwards qm:cycle-tab from before-input-event via tabStep(); View menu Back/Forward use navigationHistory.
verevonRelevance: A cheap way to give a web SPA native feel without forking the UI; Verevon should expose the same hooks (data attributes plus custom events) for its shell.
notes: Quality 3: pleasant but fragile DOM injection; limited surface. Web hotkeys Cmd/Ctrl+1-9 were removed from the browser UI (commit 0ba49de5) and exist only in the desktop preload.

name: Signed, notarized packaging path without auto-update
what: A local prototype build is produced with @electron/packager; a release build requires a Developer ID identity and notarytool profile and fails if signing or notarization fails; updates are manual.
how: package.mjs reads QM_MAC_SIGN_IDENTITY and QM_MAC_NOTARY_PROFILE, passes osxSign and osxNotarize and asar:true; npm test runs node tests and test:electron runs a real Electron navigation test with preview windows, POST popups, session sharing and sandboxing; CI runs the desktop sign-in tests in core-typecheck.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a desktop shell, add auto-update (Tauri updater or Electron autoUpdater) from day one; QM explicitly lacks it.
notes: Quality 2: signing and notarization are supported, no auto-update and unsigned Windows and Linux builds. Windows and Linux builds are unsigned prototypes.

name: Theme import from terminal and editor palettes, org branding, density
what: Users can import an iTerm2 or VS Code color theme and the UI derives readable tokens (with contrast handling); operators set the agent's name, org name, accent and mark; a density control scales rows and thinking text.
how: theme-import.ts parses palettes (iterm2|vscode) incl. JSONC, parseHex, contrast and themeTokens producing CSS variables and a dark flag; ORG_BRAND_SELF_LABEL, ORG_BRAND_ORG_NAME, ORG_BRAND_ACCENT, ORG_BRAND_MARK plus an admin Branding card; operator SVG favicons; density.ts.
verevonRelevance: A Space theming and white-label feature (Verevon already has org branding); palette import is a differentiator for power users but low priority.
notes: Quality 3: theme import and branding are useful extras; low architectural weight. Dark-mode support looks limited: only one UI file matched prefers-color-scheme or data-theme in the scout pass.

name: Accessibility present, internationalization absent
what: Many components carry ARIA attributes and focus helpers; reduced-motion is respected in a few files; the UI is English only with no i18n framework.
how: 65 web and admin files use aria-*; dialog-focus.ts, grid-nav.ts and pane-focus.ts manage focus; prefers-reduced-motion appears in 5 files; no i18next, react-intl, lingui or gettext usage and copy is inline English.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has partial nb/en i18n; QM offers no help here and is behind it.
notes: Quality 2: accessibility partial, internationalization absent. Counts are grep-based (scout pass); not re-run exhaustively.

name: Slack workspace connection managed by the platform (manifest generation and live reconciliation)
what: An operator creates the Slack app from a generated manifest or a provider-managed installation; the running Slack surface reloads when the installation record changes, rolling back to the previous configuration if the new one fails to start.
how: qm slack render/outputs generate slack-app-manifest.yml (and an SSO manifest when Slack is the OIDC provider); createSlackRuntimeReconciler() polls a versioned config every 5 s, stops the active plugin, starts the new one and on failure restarts the previous (AggregateError if both fail), with pendingCleanup for half-started sockets; Slack runs in-process, supervised by core.
verevonRelevance: The transactional adapter-activation pattern the Verevon plan lists for a future Channel Plane (version-driven reconcile with rollback) in about 100 lines.
notes: Quality 4: manifest generation and live reconciliation (test/slack-manifest.test.ts, test/slack-runtime.test.ts, test/slack-managed.test.ts); Slack only. Slack events modes: HTTP when SLACK_EVENTS_MODE=http, otherwise Socket Mode (config.ts ~1492); several Slack accounts can run side by side (SLACK_ACCOUNTS).

name: Slack as an agent surface: approvals as Run/Deny cards, task cards, deferred acknowledgement, deliveries
what: In Slack the agent answers mentions and thread follow-ups, shows an acknowledgement (reaction or emoji picked by the model), optional task and goal cards, command and credential approvals as interactive cards, and delivers results through a durable outbox that survives restarts.
how: Bolt handlers for app_mention, message, member_joined/left_channel and reactions; message-gating decides which messages start turns; approvals.ts handles hilo_ block actions with atomic claims; keychain-approvals.ts and deploy-access.ts handle keychain_ and deploy_access_ actions; turn-flow submits runs asynchronously and polls via waitRun, acks run delivery with retries (2,5,15,30 s) and relies on a poller to redeliver unacked runs; presenters render ack, task list and goal notice.
verevonRelevance: A worked example of an agent-in-chat adapter: asynchronous turn submission, progress presenters and idempotent delivery acks are what a Verevon Slack/Teams adapter would need over the Application Plane.
notes: Quality 4: most thoroughly tested adapter (52 slack-prefixed test files, e.g. test/slack-approval-cards.test.ts, test/slack-delivery.test.ts). src/slack is about 10K lines across 44 files; Slack task completion ownership is listed as a band-aid in docs/SPEC.md:52.

name: Agent mentions and addressed-versus-overheard routing in shared rooms
what: In a channel the agent distinguishes messages addressed to it (mentions, thread follow-ups it owns, DMs) from overheard chatter, and records overheard messages as clearly labelled context rather than instructions.
how: message-gating.ts (isOwnStatusCard, threadHasBotStake, mention detection) decides addressed turns; overheard messages are stored as overheard session entries with author labels; Wake situations addressed|engagedUpdate|ambientUpdate|scheduled; unmentioned thread follow-ups the agent answers are acknowledged (commit 6e8d7a80).
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space currently invokes the model on every post and has @agent mention only; QM's addressed/overheard/engaged distinction is the missing routing vocabulary for multi-human rooms.
notes: Quality 3: explicit addressed versus overheard modes (test/slack-message-gating.test.ts, test/wake-envelope.test.ts). Only gating entry points were read; the full ruleset lives in several files.

name: Self-hostable contributions model: human-written ADRs instead of code PRs
what: External contributors are asked to submit informal human-written text proposals as files in adrs/ and the maintainers implement agreed changes; bugs are reported as issues and credited.
how: CONTRIBUTING.md requires .txt or .md files under adrs/ for feature changes; the two ADRs in the tree are provider proposals (Agent37 sandbox backend, surfacing a refused agent computer); CI rejects AI co-author trailers; README offers a hosted version through a third party.
verevonRelevance: Not an architecture pattern, but it shows how QM keeps a provider-extensible contract (sandbox backends) while controlling code ownership; ADR 2 identifies a shared-layer gap (provider refusals swallowed into a generic error) worth testing in Verevon.
notes: Quality 3: an experiment in contribution policy, not architecture; the ADR folder is thin. The ADR folder is not an architecture decision log of QM's own; the real design record is docs/SPEC.md plus the wall of shame.

name: Realtime scalability stance: horizontal workers, per-session ordering, million-agent aspiration
what: QM scales by running more core and worker processes against one Postgres: per-session ordering is enforced in the queue, background work is owned by one deployment at a time, and the spec aims at swarms millions of agents strong, but there is no sharded or multi-region design.
how: Workers claim from one runs table with SKIP LOCKED; PgBouncer and pooled/direct split reduce connection pressure; swarm settings bound per-swarm agents and wall-clock; ECS blue-green cohorts; no NATS/Kafka transport, no sharding, no regional routing in src.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's NATS/Temporal stack is designed for more distribution; do not take QM's single-Postgres ceiling as a model, only its invariants.
notes: Quality 3: inference from design and absence; no load numbers published. INF from absence of other transports plus SPEC aspiration; no load numbers are published in the repo.

name: Agent-picked acknowledgement emoji and model-directed reactions
what: When a message addresses the agent, a cheap helper model picks an acknowledgement emoji from curated, default and sampled custom workspace emoji (completion-like names excluded), the pick is logged with latency, and the agent can also add real reactions when a person asks, by writing a directive in its reply.
how: createAckEmojiPicker() refreshes emoji.list hourly, builds candidates (curated + defaults + 40 random custom), calls core.pickAckEmoji(text, candidates) and records outcome picked or declined with latency; reactions are requested with [[react: name1 name2]] directives parsed and stripped from the visible reply (up to 5); agent-settable session emoji statuses exist (commit b29fda25); acknowledgement state per run is kept in a durable map and swapped as work progresses.
verevonRelevance: A low-cost 'I saw it' signal for Space rooms with many humans and agents; reactions also need a durable record of who reacted to what so agents can act on them (QM tallies reactions into the conversation view).
notes: Quality 3: cheap and tested (test/slack-ack-emoji.test.ts, test/slack-reactions.test.ts); depends on Slack emoji APIs. Depends on Slack emoji APIs; web has emoji completion only.

name: Inline reply directives parsed by the surface adapter
what: The agent triggers certain surface effects by writing small directives in its reply text (for example a reaction, or a private-continuation request); the adapter strips them from what people see, masks code regions so examples in code blocks do not fire, and applies the effects.
how: extractDirectives(reply, directiveRe, trailingRe, onMatch) masks fenced and inline code, removes matches, tidies whitespace and returns matches; REACTION_DIRECTIVE /[[react:...]]/ and the [[continue-private: task]] directive used by external audiences; trailing open directives are stripped while streaming.
verevonRelevance: A lightweight escape from tool-call overhead, but text parsing of model output is exactly what docs/SPEC.md:145-153 flags (regex lens); Verevon should prefer typed surface-effect tool calls or structured output fields.
notes: Quality 2: works and handles code regions, yet it is regex over model prose.

name: Context compaction as a logged, scope-labelled, taint-aware summary with reopen-by-sequence
what: When a conversation nears the model's context budget a summary entry replaces older turns in the model's view; the summary carries the audience label of what it summarizes, flagged security-tainted content is excluded from model context, and the agent can reopen compacted turns by sequence number with a history tool.
how: COMPACT_SOFT_FRACTION 0.7 and HARD 0.9 of a 120k-token context, recent 60 percent retained; forModelContext() keeps the latest summary and entries after throughSeq and drops thinking, text deltas, souls and turn failures; createContextSummaryPayload records throughSeq, summaryLabel scope and securityTainted; INTERRUPTED_TOOL_RESULT is substituted for tool calls cut off by a deploy; goals and memory context snapshots survive compaction.
verevonRelevance: A Space thread that spans many users and runs needs compaction that respects audience labels; QM's rule that the summary inherits the scope label (so it cannot leak to a narrower audience) is the part to copy.
notes: Quality 4: guarded compaction (test/context-compaction.test.ts) with label inheritance; breaks provider cache by design. Compaction is a first-class guarded event in the tape design; it intentionally breaks provider cache (docs/session-tape-spec.md:216-218).

name: Prompt-cache-aware context economy: stable prefixes, delta recall, lazy skills
what: The system keeps the stable part of the prompt byte-identical across turns, sends memory as a delta after the first recall in a context, orders inventories deterministically, loads skill bodies only on demand and treats every per-turn token as a cost to justify.
how: memoryRecallDelta() renders only new facts relative to the retained snapshot; commits a61db71b (stable prefixes), 3b1e3cf4 (inventories in stable order), 54c5f16a (grouped memory deltas), ca47f5c8 (recall once per context), 743b5c0d (skill contents materialized only on explicit access); SPEC 'Token performance' lens lists remaining waste (per-turn environment note, duplicated credential listings); the tape design lists four cache fast-follows (durable OpenAI cache key, split cache, settings stickiness, prefix hygiene).
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has semantic caching and cost ledgers; QM's discipline of treating prompt prefix stability and per-turn token cost as reviewed engineering concerns is a process worth adopting (a lens in code review).
notes: Quality 3: disciplined and measured (test/memory-recall-delta.test.ts, test/prompt-inventory-order.test.ts); SPEC lists remaining waste still on main. SPEC admits several items still present on main (per-turn environment note, redundant system prompt).

name: Runtime selection (harness, model, effort, speed) per scope, cron and subagent with fallback
what: The model and harness are an explicit runtime object chosen per conversation, with separate defaults for crons, subagents and a fallback, per-cron overrides, saved presets and a fast tier; provider refusals fall back along a configured ladder.
how: RuntimeChoice {harnessId, modelId, effortLevel, fastMode}; resolveRuntimeChoiceDurable() reads scope settings; RuntimePurpose cron|subagent|fallback in the config store; per-cron runtime overrides (commit 5fecef03); org runtime defaults (f7718c33); refusal fallback ladder claude-opus-5 then claude-sonnet-5 in pi-harness plus an org fallbackRuntime; typed provider errors replace regex matching (1b2d07e9).
verevonRelevance: Verevon routes models in the Model Plane; the useful structure is separate runtime purposes (interactive, scheduled, subagent, fallback) with explicit precedence, so Space scheduled agents can use cheaper settings than live chat.
notes: Quality 3: clear runtime object (test/runtime-selection.test.ts, test/runtime-purpose.test.ts) but SPEC calls four overlapping settings config-matrix growth. docs/SPEC.md:103 itself calls the four overlapping runtime settings config-matrix expansion (qm#1619, #1593, #1743).

name: Agent UX equals human UX as a design rule
what: Tool descriptions, error messages, hints and prompts are treated as the agent's interface and reviewed like UI copy; user-facing failures are translated into human-readable copy, and provider refusals are surfaced verbatim when written for a person.
how: North star 4 in the spec; failure-copy modules in core and plugins/chassis; NonRetryableTurnError carries a message meant for people; tool purposes and unambiguous action names for session, background and guidance tools (commit 8c69f826); the Agent37 ADR shows a refusal swallowed into a generic string and the proposed fix.
verevonRelevance: For the Verevon Action Catalog: design action names, parameters and error shapes for model consumption and test them with agents; surface owner-plane refusals verbatim when they are written for a human.
notes: Quality 3: a stated principle with real code behind it (test/failure-copy.test.ts); hard to measure.

name: Agent room I/O as one explicit tool: post here, reach elsewhere, react, edit own, read thread, what is new, search, members, files
what: In ambient and coordinator turns the agent has no implicit voice: it speaks only by calling one surface tool, and ending a turn without a post means silence. The tool separates replying in this conversation (post) from sending to a different audience (reach) and gives the agent read primitives over the room it is in.
how: A tool named after the surface (slack, or the web surface name) with actions post, reach, react, edit, delete, read_thread, whats_new, search, read_members and read_file. post rejects any channel, recipient or participants argument (post_cannot_address) so a reply cannot turn into a broadcast; reach requires exactly one of channel, recipient or participants, resolves it through the acting human's membership and is capped at 5 outbound posts per turn. search takes source mirror (the local message cache) or source slack (runs as the asking person through their own login). Turns receive the tool when surfaceTools is set: ambient workers spawned by the judge (idempotency key ambient:<org>:<surface>:<container>:<latestTs>) and flagged coordinator turns; run-result delivery does not auto-post their final text. Ordinary addressed turns post the final reply text.
verevonRelevance: Gives Space agents an explicit typed room API (reply, send elsewhere, react, read history, members and files) instead of 'the final text is the post', which makes silence, audience choice and audit first-class; map the actions to Application-plane message projections gated by Control membership.
notes: Quality 4: explicit post versus reach split with typed errors (test/surface-read-tools.test.ts, test/surface-post-files.test.ts); used only for ambient and coordinator turns. Only ambient and coordinator turns use it today. The tool text tells the agent not to quote the asker's private search hits into a room; that is a prompt rule and its enforcement was not traced (INF).

name: Per-speaker AI account: bring your own API key or subscription login, with no silent fallback to company access
what: A person can connect their own Anthropic or OpenAI API key, or sign in with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription, and an org can require this. In any room the person who spoke runs on their own account; if it is unavailable the turn stops with a reconnect message instead of using company credentials.
how: The config store holds a per-person model account (company, personal, openai or anthropic) and an org-level individual-model-auth requirement; the user-model-auth routes connect API keys and run Claude and ChatGPT logins; OAuth tokens live in the keychain with single-flight refresh and a turn only receives derived access and id tokens, never the refresh token. resolveIndividualAuthRouting() chooses provider and harness (API key goes to pi, Claude OAuth to the claude harness, ChatGPT OAuth to codex or to pi through the Codex provider) and refuses fast or overlay models that need an API key. loadRuntimeAuth() applies it only to live human turns, never to external audiences, and throws a non-retryable error when the personal route cannot be built. The account applies only to human-origin turns (background, cron and external turns stay on company access); the choice is stamped on the submitted run, a message under a different account queues separately, and a steer is refused with account_changed when the viewer's account differs from the run's.
verevonRelevance: Verevon meters cost per org; charging and rate-limiting the speaking person with their own account would let a Space support personal agents on personal quota, but reusing subscription logins needs a vendor-terms review before any copy.
notes: Quality 3: complete routing and no-fallback rule (test/personal-model-account.test.ts, test/personal-model-account-execution.test.ts); depends on vendor OAuth clients. INF (medium): CLAUDE_CLIENT_ID and CHATGPT_CLIENT_ID in subscription-oauth.ts look like the public OAuth clients of the vendors' own command-line tools; no vendor permission is stated in the files read. Claude subscription access is refused for browser inference.

name: Agent browser as a skill: remote CDP browser, embedded runner, profile held as a keychain credential, DM-only sign-ins
what: The agent can act on websites in a hosted stealth browser. The logic is a seed skill, the browser runs at a third-party provider, a person's signed-in profile is a secret in their keychain, and a sign-in wall is handed to the person as a live-view link.
how: skills-seed/browse/SKILL.md has the agent drive a remote browser over CDP (Kernel, Anchor or Browserbase, chosen by which API key exists; a new provider is a provider doc plus an org credential, with no core change) using browser-use baked into the sandbox image. Org provider keys arrive as sandbox env; a person's own key and profile name arrive only through keychain handles named on execute. Profiles and sign-in links are DM-only: in a channel the browser runs profile-less and declines account tasks. The runner prints a typed outcome (done, or signin_needed with the wall URL); the agent checks the URL against the task's domain, hands the person the LIVE_VIEW link, waits, then re-runs. CDP_URL is treated as a secret and the browser is deleted at the end.
verevonRelevance: Closest QM analogue to Grok Bot's own-browser agent; a Space agent needs a hosted browser plus per-person sign-in hand-off, and Verevon should keep Quarry as executor and evidence owner while adopting the DM-only profile rule, the typed signin_needed outcome and live-view takeover.
notes: Quality 3: works through prompts and a baked runner; no technical gate and a pinned third-party library with known flaky behaviour. Guarded by prompt text, not a technical boundary (see the browser gates record). The skill pins browser-use 0.12.9 and documents two known flaky behaviours.

name: Browser model grant: the browser runner calls back to core with a scoped token, so the browser vendor never holds a model key
what: The inner browser agent needs an LLM; instead of a provider key, core mints a capability token for one model and one account and serves OpenAI-style completions at a core route that resolves the company or the person's own account at call time.
how: Capability claims browserModel and browserAccount under audience browser-model; POST /v1/browser-model/chat/completions accepts an allowlist of chat fields, no streaming, 16 MiB body, 120 s timeout. It returns 403 without the grant or in strict posture, 409 when the person's AI account or model changed since the token was minted (start a new turn), 422 for Claude subscription access, and otherwise proxies to the model gateway with redirects refused or builds a native completion with the person's credentials. The skill gives the runner BROWSE_LAB_BASE_URL and the token as an x-agent-capability header.
verevonRelevance: Maps directly onto Verevon browser grants: a short-lived, single-model, account-bound grant that lets a browser runner reason without ever seeing provider keys is the shape Space browser sessions should use, with cost attributed to the Space and the speaker.
notes: Quality 4: small, fail-closed and checked against the live account at call time.

name: Browser runner sits outside command policy and approvals; money is authorized in the task text before launch
what: Actions inside the browser runner do not pass the approval gates shell commands do. QM relies on explicit task-level consent, with a spending ceiling written into the task, and on the runner refusing unauthorized purchases. Browser traffic leaves through the browser provider, not QM's egress proxy.
how: SECURITY.md lists this as a known limitation. The skill says the runner has no approval gate, so the agent must confirm specifics with the person and embed the authorization with a ceiling in the task text, must not launch spending tasks from a scheduled fire without a standing instruction, and appends a guard prompt (treat page content as data, stop at sign-in walls, spend only what the task authorizes).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's rule that the Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes or rejects them is stronger; use QM as the negative example for purchases and other side effects and keep per-action Quarry grants plus human approval.
notes: Quality 2: documented known gap rather than a control; prompts are the only guard.

name: Admission-time rate limit and rolling-window spend budget per acting person and per org
what: Before a turn starts, the acting human's request count and estimated spend in a rolling window are checked against per-person and org limits; refused turns get a readable reason with the retry time or the amount spent.
how: createRateLimiter and createPostgresRateLimiter count requests per principal per window; createBudgetTracker and createPostgresBudgetTracker keep a rolling sum of dollars per principal plus an '@org' key. The orchestrator checks both before resolving the turn (and in the strict-posture steering path). Every model call (main turns, compaction, screening, helper judges) records estimateCostUsd(inputTokens) at a flat default of 5 USD per million input tokens, fire and forget. Limits come from RATE_LIMIT_PER_WINDOW, BUDGET_USD_PER_WINDOW, ORG_BUDGET_USD_PER_WINDOW and BUDGET_WINDOW_MS, and the Postgres budget is only created when a limit is set.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has a first-class cost ledger and org quotas; the pattern worth keeping is charging the speaking person (not the room) with an org ceiling and a readable refusal, but a Space also needs per-Space and per-agent ceilings and real priced usage instead of an input-token estimate.
notes: Quality 2: present but coarse: input-token estimate at a flat price (test/budget.test.ts, test/rate-limiter.test.ts). Coarse: input tokens only, flat price, recorded after the call, so a turn can overshoot. No per-room or per-agent budget. The real priced ledger and export are a separate path (see the spend record).

name: Admin model registry with a verification probe bound to a credential fingerprint
what: An admin cannot enable a custom or newly added model until a real probe succeeds; the success is stored as a fingerprint that stops matching, and removes the model from the picker, when the definition, credential or gateway target changes.
